title: Can Dodgers Afford To Put Shohei Ohtani On Injured List?
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are trying to secure a first round bye, but some of their stars are struggling
fullText:
Shohei Ohtani has been dealing with some injuries that have kept him off the mound since July 3, but now his swing is starting to look like it's also being impacted.

Ohtani has been dealing with a knee injury and a right biceps issue. The injuries have shut him down from pitching, but he has not complained about it hurting his offense. However, on Wednesday, he struck out four times in four at-bats and Dave Roberts noted that he does not look right.

"I think that tonight was kind of the tip of the iceberg," Roberts said after Wednesday's game, per MLB.com's Sonja Chen. "But I've seen it over the last couple weeks, where he hasn't been who he is."

Per Chen, Roberts does not think Ohtani will need to go on the injured list. However, some days off are not off the table.

Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand!

"Is a day or two -- or I mean, shoot, even 10 days, is that going to help get him to be 100%? Don't know the answer," Roberts said. "But I think where we're at, I think he's just going to have to find a way to make do and do the best he can. But what can I do? Have the conversation. Get him off his feet. Kind of try to get some strength back. Get him feeling better, and then run him out there."

The real question is whether the Dodgers can even afford to put him on the injured list. Their offense scored the sixth-fewest runs in baseball in August, and they are not off to the best start in September. Ohtani has been part of the problem, hitting .137 with a .545 OPS in his last 13 games.

However, if they put him on the injured list, they may not even have someone better to replace him. Dalton Rushing could serve as the designated hitter with Ohtani out, but he struggles against lefties and is not the same threat in the lineup that Ohtani is. They could look to call up James Tibbs III, but relying on a rookie while they fight for postseason positioning is less than ideal.

The reality is, the Dodgers do not need the bye to win the World Series. They can 100% afford to place Ohtani on the injured list, but they may not play great. However, it's unlikely they finish lower than the No. 3 seed. They won the World Series as a No. 3 seed last year.

Their rotation is capable of carrying them in October, even without Ohtani. Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are a four-man rotation that no team in the postseason would feel comfortable against.

title: Yankees’ Cam Schlittler makes MLB history, joining Randy Johnson as only other pitcher to accomplish feat
description: Cam Schlittler continues to be a revelation.
fullText:
New York Yankees starting pitcher Cam Schlittler has accomplished something rarely seen on an MLB mound.

He joins Randy Johnson as the only modern-era pitcher to produce a streak of this length while striking out more batters than hits allowed on the road.

MORE: Yankees, Aaron Boone announce new pitching plans for weekend series in San Diego

Aug 21, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees starting pitcher Cam Schlittler (31) pitches against the Toronto Blue Jays during the first inning at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Schlittler delivered another dominant performance in the Yankees' 6-3 victory over the Los Angeles Angels last night. The right-hander struck out nine batters while allowing just two hits across eight innings, continuing what has become an extraordinary run away from New York.

With his latest outing, Schlittler has now recorded more strikeouts than hits allowed in each of his last 21 road starts. The streak dates back to August 2, 2025, and during that span, the Yankees sophomore has struck out 157 batters while surrendering only 70 hits.

That puts Schlittler in rare company. The only other pitcher in the modern era to achieve a streak of at least this length was Johnson, who accomplished the feat across 23 games with the Arizona Diamondbacks from 1999 to 2000.

MORE: Padres made a huge mistake & are paying for it now

Schlittler's historic road stretch is just one part of an impressive sophomore campaign. The Yankees starter has emerged as a legitimate contender for the American League Cy Young Award, posting a 2.04 ERA and 0.94 WHIP alongside a 12-6 record through 29 starts.

His consistency has also played a major role in keeping the Yankees firmly in the American League playoff picture. New York currently holds the first Wild Card spot with an 80-60 record and a 9.5-game cushion.

The Yankees will now turn their attention toward a weekend series in San Diego against the Padres. With Schlittler continuing to pitch at an elite level, New York has another major weapon as it looks to secure its postseason position.

If his historic road dominance continues, Schlittler could finish the season not only as one of the Yankees' most important players, but also as one of the American League's premier starting pitchers.

title: Fantasy Football Roundtable: 3 late-round sleeper tight ends our analysts are targeting in 2026 drafts
description: Here are some tight ends who could surprise in 2026 fantasy football.
fullText:
Many fantasy football managers will employ a late-round TE strategy going into their drafts. Once you get past the handful of elite options at TE, things get pretty flat pretty quick. With that in mind, Yahoo analysts Hayden Winks, Justin Boone and Scott Pianowski give you their favorite sleeper tight end for the 2026 season.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

If you want the most terminally online deep sleeper, Ferguson is your guy. The 2025 second-round pick played in the most absurd role in tight end history last year under coach Sean McVay. Ferguson largely played a vertical receiving role in 2- and 3-TE sets as a downfield receiver in disguise. His average depth of target was 17.9 yards downfield. Only Tyquan Thornton, Alec Pierce and Kyle Williams were targeted more downfield!!! That will boggle the mind. Fast-forward to this year, the Rams need better talent at "WR," and Ferguson could be the answer based on what he provided last season. Davante Adams was dangled in trade discussions open to the public after a down season beyond the goal line, and trading for Tutu Atwell on Aug. 27 is never a great sign for the rest of the room. There's a chance (25%) that Ferguson is viewed as the team's WR3 this season. McVay's done crazy things like this before with Puka Nacua, Cooper Kupp, Kyren Williams, Blake Corum and 3-TE sets. — Hayden Winks

The loss of a true breakout receiver in Jayden Higgins will have significant ramifications on the Texans' passing attack. Nico Collins is an elite top target, with Jaylin Noel and Kayshon Boutte as quality contributors. However, fantasy managers shouldn't sleep on Dalton Schultz. The veteran tight end seems like a boring pick, but he's quietly coming off a strong fantasy campaign where he averaged the 11th-most points at his position over the final 13 weeks. That included finishing tied for third in receptions among tight ends (82) and sixth in receiving yards (777). With Higgins sidelined for the season, Schultz now has a chance to be C.J. Stroud's No. 2 target once again. You're not going to impress your leaguemates by taking the 30-year-old Texans tight end. But if you somehow miss out on the top-13 options at the position, Schultz is in the next group of high-end TE2s who could easily end the year as a fantasy TE1. — Justin Boone

Normally it would feel like a major cheat to list someone like Johnson as a sleeper, but so long as his Yahoo ADP lags outside 120, it's my job to scream his name from the masses. Johnson is coming off a handy 77-catch, 889-yard season, and his touchdown equity will probably rise given a full year from QB Tyler Shough (who spent one year with Johnson at Oregon). With Jordyn Tyson down for two months, Johnson opens the year as the second option in a rising New Orleans offense, helmed by Shough and shrewd offensive designer Kellen Moore. It doesn't matter how you approach the tight end spot, Johnson is a legitimate TE1 in medium and deeper leagues, and a dynamite TE2 if you play in a shallower format. He's been mispriced all summer, so keep taking advantage.

If you get sniped on Johnson, Jaguars TE Brenton Strange about a round later is a nice consolation prize. Leave the light on for him, too. — Scott Pianowski

title: Chicago Fire acquire Noah Allen from Inter Miami
description: TRACKER STATUS: LoanChicago Fire FC have acquired defender Noah Allen on loan from Inter Miami CF, the clubs announced Thursday.The 22-year-old Greek youth international's l...
fullText:
Chicago Fire FC have acquired defender Noah Allen on loan from Inter Miami CF, the clubs announced Thursday.

The 22-year-old Greek youth international's loan is through the 2026 MLS season with a permanent trade option.

Allen will occupy a U22 Initiative roster slot for Chicago.

"As a young defender who has developed through the MLS ranks, Noah has consistently shown that he can compete at the highest levels of Major League Soccer," said Chicago director of football and head coach Gregg Berhalter.

"What stands out is his competitive mentality, his drive to improve and his versatile skill set. He has valuable experience for his age, and we believe he has the qualities to make an impact on this team."

Allen is Inter Miami's all-time appearances leader, featuring 132 times and contributing 3g/7a. He came through Inter Miami's academy before signing a homegrown deal in 2022.

During his time with the Herons, Allen helped the club win Leagues Cup, Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup titles. In 2025, he finished No. 12 on the league's 22 Under 22 Rankings.

"I'm thankful to have been a part of Inter Miami and its history, and to have seen the Club grow into what it is today," said Allen. "I'm just grateful that I was able to be a part of it. To everyone who helped me and for all the memories I made, I'll cherish them with me forever."

Allen continues a busy summer transfer deadline for Chicago, who have added Georgian international midfielder Anzor Mekvabishvili, Norwegian international defender Andreas Hanche-Olsen and former US youth international midfielder Johan Gómez in recent days.

Meanwhile, former Spain international Sergio Reguilón is Miami's top left back upon Allen's exit.

title: Carlos Alcaraz planning more breaks in ‘impossible’ tennis schedule
description: Carlos Alcaraz has taken a swipe at the hectic tennis calendar and said he will skip tournaments from now on. Alcaraz is making his comeback from more than four months out with a wrist injury to defend his US Open title.
fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz has taken a swipe at the hectic tennis calendar and said he will skip tournaments from now on.

Alcaraz is making his comeback from more than four months out with a wrist injury to defend his US Open title.

The Spaniard pointed to the absences of other top stars as evidence that the schedule is too demanding and will keep causing injuries.

World number one Jannik Sinner and British star Jack Draper are notable absentees at Flushing Meadows along with Holger Rune, Joao Fonseca and a host of other players.

"I took more (time off) than I wanted, to be honest, but you know, seeing how tight is the calendar, obviously I don't want to have this break because (of) an injury," said Alcaraz after coming from a set down to beat Jaime Faria in the second round.

"But in the future, I'm going to take some breaks, some long breaks. Maybe not four months, but one month, two months, missing some tournaments, because it's impossible to play them all.

"I think they (are) adding more important tournaments. You know, in a way they (are) making us play. You can say 'no'. You can keep one or two.

"You can decide your calendar, but there are some Masters 1000s, some grand slams, and we've been out playing 40 weeks if we got to play every mandatory tournament that the ATP, you know, required us to play.

"So it's impossible, and we are seeing a lot of players getting injured, a lot of players getting tired. If they don't do anything about it, we are going to see even 

"But for me, taking this break because (of) an injury, it wasn't that good, but you know, what I'm going to say is I'm going to take some breaks and miss some tournaments in the future, for sure."

Alcaraz plays Chinese world number 113 Wu Yibing in round three on Friday.

PITTSBURGH — Ahead of Thursday's bullpen game against the Giants, the Pirates have recalled right-handed pitcher Wilber Dotel from Triple-A Indianapolis. Left-handed pitcher Evan Sisk was optioned to Indianapolis as the corresponding move.

This will be Dotel's fifth stint with the Pirates this season after going 1-4 with a 4.71 ERA in 15 relief appearances through the first four. In 28.2 big-league innings, the 23-year-old has allowed 15 earned runs on 27 hits with 13 walks and 31 strikeouts.

In 12 appearances/five starts with Indianapolis this season, Dotel is 5-3 with a 4.50 ERA and 33 strikeouts in 36 innings.

Sisk pitched for the Pirates on Tuesday and was charged with three runs after walking three batters and only recording one out. The 29-year-old is 1-0 with a 3.16 ERA in 39 big-league appearances this season. In his last seven appearances dating back to Aug. 5, Sisk has an 8.53 ERA.

title: CEO explains why former Gunner pulled out of deadline-day transfer
description: Folarin Balogun’s transfer to Everton fell apart at the last minute on transfer deadline day, and AS Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro has explained why.Photo by VALERY HACHE/AFP via Getty ImagesOn transfer d...
fullText:
On transfer deadline day, AS Monaco's Folarin Balogun was set to sign for Everton in a €50m package that would see Arsenal cashing in on their 17.5% sell-on clause.

Yet that move was thrown into doubt amid reports that Balogun had failed his medical.

After further review, Everton ultimately still wanted to proceed with the deal, and it looked to be going ahead. But the player pulled out at the last minute, and initial reports didn't explain why.

Speaking to the media, Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro gave his version of events, and he explained why Balogun decided not to go ahead with the transfer.

"We had a clear agreement for Balogun to go to Everton," Scuro revealed (via BBC Sport). "Balogun flew yesterday morning to complete his medical and sign a contract. Everything was going pretty well. Around 19:00 we were contacted by Everton, who raised concerns about Balogun's medical.

"It took around two or three hours to go through the assessments, consult other doctors and review the scans. Around 22:00 our time, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised there was no issue and decided they were ready to sign the contract.

"I signed the contract. Everton signed the contract. At the last moment, the player decided not to sign.

"Basically, Balogun's position was: 'I'm not feeling comfortable with the way the club treated me. I'm not comfortable with the doubts raised about my future or my health. I have no issue, so I'm not comfortable signing a contract here.'"

That's a fair position to take, particularly as Balogun's 'failed medical' had immediately leaked to the media. Everton clearly made no efforts to keep the news quiet, despite the impact it could have on the public perception of the player.

Arsenal will retain their sell-on clause for future windows, but whether Monaco receive another bid for a similar amount is far from certain. The striker's deal expires in 2028, and he won't have a World Cup to showcase his talents again next summer.

Unless the 25-year-old has a fantastic 2026/27 season, it's likely a transfer next year won't hit the same figure in that context.

title: Sarr needs time to process collapse of Liverpool move
description: Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr will need time to process the collapse of his proposed move to Liverpool, says Eagles head coach Pierre Sage.
fullText:
Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr will need time to process the collapse of his proposed move to Liverpool, says head coach Pierre Sage.

The Senegal attacker, who was the club's top scorer last season, was linked with a move to Anfield late in the transfer window, but ended up staying at Selhurst Park.

Sage admitted: "He has to digest for sure because it's a dream for a lot of players to play with this kind of club (Liverpool).

"He had a good opportunity but in the end it didn't work. If he wants to continue, you have to have a good season with us as he did last year. We know he needs time.

"Like every bad situation, time does the job and we need time for that."

Sarr, 28, has yet to feature for Palace this season, missing Premier League defeats at Everton and home to Manchester City with a groin injury. He will remain sidelined for Saturday's trip to Fulham (15:00 BST).

With uncertainty over Sarr's future, Palace were in talks with Belgium forward Malick Fofana on deadline day, but the 21-year-old chose to leave Lyon for Sunderland in a deal worth £30m.

"We gave our best," added Frenchman Sage on the negotiations. "At the end of the day the player chose his criteria and I wish him and them the best because he's a good guy and a good player."

Saturday's opponents Fulham are also seeking their first Premier League point after losing their first two games, at home to Chelsea and away at Sunderland.

title: Ben Stokes clean bowled: Watch Yuzvendra Chahal dismiss Ex-England captain in County game with a peach of a delivery
description: Yuzvendra Chahal clean-bowled Ben Stokes with a stunning spinning delivery in the County Championship, finishing with 4/36 for Northamptonshire.
fullText:
Ben Stokes clean bowled: Watch Yuzvendra Chahal dismiss Ex-England captain in County game with a peach of a delivery originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Yuzvendra Chahal bowled Ben Stokes with a sharply turning leg-break during a County Championship clash for Northamptonshire.

Chahal finished with impressive figures of 4/36 as Durham were bundled out for 205 in the innings.

Stokes has now struggled twice against Indian spinners in county cricket, previously dismissed cheaply by Sai Kishore too.

Yuzvendra Chahal conjured up a beauty in the County Championship, ripping through Ben Stokes' defence and sending his stumps flying.

Chahal, who is playing for Northamptonshire against Durham in Division Two, got his man in the 47th over, with Durham wobbling at 187 for six at the County Ground in Northampton. Stokes had managed 14 before the leg-spin veteran worked his magic.

Coming around the wicket, Chahal tossed one up outside off. Stokes read the line well enough and went for the defensive shot. The ball landed outside off and then spun back sharply into the left-hander, and Stokes' bat simply didn't come down in time to shut the gap between bat and pad. Through it went, crashing straight into the top of off stump.

All Stokes could do was stand there, staring at the pitch like it had betrayed him, before trudging back to the pavilion.

That is sensational pic.twitter.com/ChwDk7JfLR

That wicket wasn't a one-off for Chahal as it was his third scalp of the innings and the cherry on top of a fantastic spell. By the time he was done, his figures read 4/36 from 15.2 overs, and Durham were eventually bowled out for 205 in 56.2 overs.

David Bedingham was the standout with the bat for Durham, top-scoring with 81 off 91 deliveries. Mayank Agarwal chipped in with 36, while Alex Lees managed 24 before he too fell to Chahal.

This wasn't the first time Indian spin has got the better of Stokes in county cricket recently, either. In an earlier match against Gloucestershire, he'd looked in decent touch, cruising to 45 off just 43 balls with seven fours and a six to his name, until Sai Kishore stepped in and cut that innings short.

Compared to that dismissal, though, what Chahal produced was on another level altogether, as the ball had sharper turn, better disguise, and a delivery that beat both Stokes' reading of the ball and his defensive technique in one go.

title: Missed opportunities doom Twins in 4-hour, 12-inning, 41-player marathon
description: Wednesday's game at Target Field had everything — except a Twins victory.
fullText:
Wednesday night's series finale between the Twins and Tigers at Target Field had a little bit of everything. After the Twins dominated the first two games of the series by a combined 26-3 margin, this one was far more competitive and required over four hours to determine a winner. Ultimately, missed opportunities at the plate doomed Minnesota in an 11-6 loss in 12 innings.

The game ran four hours and nine minutes, making it the longest Twins game of the season by over half an hour — and the sixth-longest game in all of MLB in 2026. It's the third-longest game the Twins have played in during the four years of the pitch clock era.

20 players start every baseball game. Another 21 came off the bench in this game. There were 13 relief pitchers used (seven for the Twins, six for the Tigers) and eight position players off the bench. Excluding their other four starting pitchers, the Twins used 21 of the 24 players available to them in this game.

Some other numbers: There were 23 hits in the game, nine walks (two of them intentional), 28 strikeouts, four hit-by-pitches, 10 ABS challenges, 24 runners left on base, and 406 pitches thrown.

The Tigers jumped out to a 2-0 lead in the second inning on a two-run double by John Peck, his first major league hit, off of Dean Kremer. The Twins didn't have a hit against Drew Anderson until Ryan Jeffers' RBI double in the fourth. Detroit immediately responded with two runs in the top of the fifth off of Kremer and Kody Funderburk, then went up 5-1 in the sixth.

But the Twins had a comeback in them. Trevor Larnach drove in a run with a double in the bottom of the sixth. In the eighth, Minnesota loaded the bases with one out, then watched Kenley Jansen walk Victor Caratini to force in a run. One batter later, Royce Lewis worked a great at-bat and then ripped a ball that got past Peck at shortstop for a game-tying two-run single.

TIE GAME!!! pic.twitter.com/zbUlBRSok9

After the Lewis hit, the Twins still had runners at second and third with only one out. All rookie shortstop Kaelen Culpepper needed to do was put the ball in play somewhere that would allow Ryan Kreidler to score from third. He couldn't do it.

Culpepper fouled off a Jansen cutter right down the middle to begin the at-bat, didn't challenge a pitch that just missed the inside edge but was called for strike two, and did challenge (unsuccessfully) a perfect cutter that caught the inside part of the plate for strike three. The Tigers then brought in lefty Tyler Holton, who struck Walker Jenkins out on four pitches to escape the jam. Culpepper and Jenkins have very bright futures, but they were a combined 0 for 9 with five strikeouts in this game.

The game went to extra innings, and the Twins got off to a great start when Yoendrys Gomez stranded the automatic runner at second base in the top half of the tenth. To begin the bottom half, recent call-up Ben Ross came up for his second MLB plate appearance. His job was to bunt Ryan Jeffers over to third base. But Ross's bunt popped into the air and Jeffers took a couple steps back towards the bag, thinking it might get caught. That meant Jeffers wasn't able to advance when the ball did land fair.

After a Kreidler walk, Lewis struck out on three pitches and Culpepper flew out to the warning track in right field.

The Tigers got a Max Clark RBI double to lead off the top of the 11th, but Taylor Rogers was able to prevent any further damage from there. In the bottom of the inning, Luke Keaschall's RBI single tied it at 6-6, and Brooks Lee followed him with a single that put runners on the corners with one out.

Knowing anything hit to the outfield would likely end the game, Tigers manager A.J. Hinch went to a five-man infield against Kody Clemens. All the Twins needed was a grounder through a hole, a bloop hit, or a sacrifice fly. But while Clemens battled against Kyle Finnegan, he ultimately struck out on the eighth pitch of the at-bat. Jeffers then bounced out to shortstop to send the game to a 12th frame.

The top of the 12th is where the Twins' missed opportunities came back to haunt them. Spencer Torkelson led off with a two-run homer off of a hanging slider from Tommy Nance. The Tigers then loaded the bases with two outs on a single, walk, and HBP, setting up a Javier Baez bases-clearing bloop double off of Lewis's glove behind first base.

JAVY CLEARS THE BASES pic.twitter.com/GigkgH2l3N

The Twins went down in order in the bottom half of the 12th.

"We gave ourselves a bunch of opportunities and unfortunately, we weren't able to capitalize on those opportunities," Twins manager Derek Shelton said. "We had a chance to win the game at multiple spots."

It was also a missed opportunity for the Twins (67-73) to gain ground in the AL wild card race on the Guardians, Rangers, and Orioles, who all lost earlier on Wednesday. The silver lining is that they didn't lose any ground. They remain 3.5 games back of Cleveland for the final playoff spot.

The Twins are off Thursday and then will begin another stretch of six straight games against the White Sox and Tigers — this time, on the road in Chicago and Detroit. Minnesota would need to go 14-8 in its final 22 games to finish .500. 15 or more wins may be needed to reach the playoffs.

We are in the age of big media consolidation and content networks. But even with the proliferation of AI, nothing can beat the quality and inherent knowledge of local sports journalism. Our writing room consists of a Tommy, a Gopher, and even a Mustang. We know the Minnesota towns and the great names that played on its diamonds, courts, fields or rinks. title: London City shirt deal biggest in women's game - Kang
description: London City Lionesses owner Michele Kang says they have signed the biggest shirt sponsorship deal in the women's game.
fullText:
London City Lionesses owner Michelle Kang says her club's new shirt sponsorship deal with sports brand Nike is the largest in the women's game - and worth more than those of some Premier League sides.

The current largest deal for a women's side is believed to be for the new National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) franchise in Atlanta, which is set to join the competition in 2028.

Atlanta's shirt deal is reportedly worth about $4m (£2.96m), a similar figure to that of new entrants to the Premier League and more than most Championship clubs.

"I can absolutely confirm that this is the largest women only front of shirt deal," Kang told BBC Sport. "It is higher than the Atlanta number."

The news comes after a big summer for London City which has seen them sign two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas and Spain defender Mapi Leon from Barcelona, as well as ex-England goalkeeper Mary Earps and Lyon winger Kadidiatou Diani.

Unmasking London City's Spanish superstar

Media Day Diaries: Inside London City Lionesses

Kang added: "There are so many other people who believe in the future of women's football. They didn't make this decision lightly - they did not write a charity cheque. They believe in the future and they believe together we will invest and build this future together."

All Women's Super League clubs apart from London City share shirt sponsors with their men's teams.

London City's record is only for independent women's clubs, of which they are the only one in England's top flight.

Kang took over London City in 2023 and has shaken up the WSL, spending big to get the team to the top flight. They then finished sixth in the division last year.

She also owns Lyon in France and Washington Spirit in the United States.

They host Manchester United in the first match of the Women's Super League season on Friday (19:00 BST) and will have a capacity crowd at the Copperjax Community Stadium in Bromley, with over 5,400 tickets sold for the match.

Kang has previously told BBC Sport she has long-term ambitions of bringing success to the club and they "have an aspiration to be at the top of the game".

title: Bengals plan to use Erick All Jr. with no restrictions in Week 1
description: Bengals coach Zac Taylor says tight end Erick All Jr. will not be limited when he returns from his lengthy ACL recovery in Week 1.
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bengals have taken a cautious approach with Erick All Jr. during training camp.

They apparently won't be doing the same when the regular season begins, as head coach Zac Taylor indicated there are no plans to put All on a limited workload when Cincinnati opens its season against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic presented Taylor with two possibilities for handling All early in the season. One would be giving him a full workload with no reservations. The other would be gradually expanding his role based on how his knee responds.

"The first one," Taylor said. "The first one."

That was welcome news for All, who admitted he had been concerned the Bengals might continue restricting him after he played only six preseason snaps.

"Honestly, I had no idea," All said, via The Athletic. "I kind of got worried they were going to (limit me). I'm glad they are not doing that."

All tore his ACL in November 2024, and complications from the injury kept him sidelined for the entire 2025 season. Cincinnati gradually increased his workload after he was cleared this offseason.

The 25-year-old said he feels "100 percent, for sure," although he acknowledged his knee still feels different on some days.

Getting All back without restrictions would give Cincinnati a compelling wrinkle offensively. His combination of blocking and receiving ability allowed the Bengals to operate more frequently from under center and utilize play action during his rookie season.

Now, Taylor appears ready to find out how much All can add to the offense.

title: Arrest made in break-in at home of Eagles RB Saquon Barkley
description: An arrest has been made in connection with the attempted burglary at the home of Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley.
fullText:
An arrest has been made in connection with the attempted burglary at the home of Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley.

The Montgomery County District Attorney's Office announced Wednesday that 24-year-old Jabir Parker of Philadelphia has been arrested in connection with the crime.

Parker faces multiple felony charges, including burglary, conspiracy to burglarize, criminal trespass (breaking into a structure) and other related offenses.

Authorities allege Parker broke into Barkley's home in Tredyffrin Township, Chester County, during the early morning hours of July 18.

According to investigators, Barkley and his family were inside the home at the time of the burglary, but no one was injured.

"In this neighborhood, it's a rare thing. Saquon is somebody who, whenhe moved to the neighborhood, was very kind to the kids. It's heartbreaking when someone like that just wants to be left alone," said Daryl Williams of Tredyfrin Township.

RELATED | Suspects sought in burglary at Saquon Barkley's Malvern home

Suspects sought in burglary at Saquon Barkley's Malvern home

Prosecutors said Parker is also accused of stealing nearly $1 million worth of jewelry during burglaries at two homes in Montgomery County.

One of the burglaries happened on June 22 in Bryn Mawr. The investigation found that 12 pieces of jewelry, with an estimated value of $106,700, were stolen.

Another burglary happened on July 5 at a home in Wynnewood. Police say 28 items of jewelry worth an estimated $687,292 were stolen, as well as a safe.

The homeowners were not home during either of those two cases.

Detectives used cellphone location data, commonly known as geofencing, to link Parker's phone to the crime scenes, according to authorities.

Police say the SUV used as a getaway was returned to a rental company an hour and a half after fleeing Barkley's home.

Detectives say Parker also Googled phrases like, "Do touchscreen gloves leave fingerprints" and "rental car." And after the burglaries, he allegedly Googled what he stole, including a Rolex watch just 53 minutes after the theft.

He is currently being held on a $1 million cash bond.

Investigators are still looking for two to three other suspects involved in these crimes.

title: Why Michael Penix Jr. has 'won' the Falcons QB job, regardless of Week 1
description: The Falcons don't have a starting QB named yet, but Michael Penix Jr. still "won" the job.
fullText:
The Atlanta Falcons quarterback battle might not be much of a battle at all.

According to NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe, the Falcons plan to "eventually" start Michael Penix Jr. to get a good look at him before the 2027 NFL Draft, even if quarterback Tua Tagovailoa starts in Week 1 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. This would support previous scuttlebutt that Tagovailoa was on shaky footing in Atlanta.

In a Wednesday segment, Wolfe referred to Tagovailoa as a "placeholder" and said that the Falcons "want to see more of Penix. The plan is for [Penix] to start eventually."

Wolfe added that the team doesn't want to rush Penix back from his 2025 ACL injury, so that might be why Tagovailoa starts to season for the Falcons before Penix rejoins the lineup.

However, it still sounds like both options are on the table for Atlanta leading up into that Sept. 13 season opener at Pittsburgh.

Falcons new regime: president of 🏈 Matt Ryan, HC Kevin Stefanski & GM Ian Cunningham will be collaborative in QB1 decision. 

But it’s prove it time for Penix & Tua with 2027 draft decision in deeper QB class looming: pic.twitter.com/h6GUzyuyXr

With the Falcons the only organization in the NFL still undecided on a 2026 starter, we'll see if Penix is healthy and comfortable enough to claim the job, or if Tagovailoa holds down the fort until Penix is ready. Unless Tagovailoa absolutely balls out in the event he starts, it's just hard to see anybody but Penix as the clear winner in this battle.

If Penix plays well, it's possible he keeps Atlanta from drafting a 2027 rookie. If he doesn't, the Falcons almost feel locked into adding somebody else next spring.

It's possible, but the team looks destined to choose between Penix and Tagovailoa for Week 1.

title: How Cubs might've made their bullpen 'worse' with one Angels trade
description: This move from the Cubs has not worked out at-all this season.
fullText:
How Cubs might've made their bullpen 'worse' with one Angels trade originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Chicago Cubs made a few additions at the 2026 MLB trade deadline, adding Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes, and Tyrone Taylor to improve the rotation and outfield depth.

But they also added a reliever, swinging a trade with the Los Angeles Angels for Ryan Zeferjahn, a flame-throwing righty who had a 3.66 ERA for the Angels in 45 outings before the deadline deal.

However, as Joel Reuter of Bleacher Report highlighted, the aftermath of that trade might've actually made the Cubs' bullpen "worse" given how poorly Zeferjahn has pitched for the Cubs since the trade.

"The Cubs made their bullpen worse," Reuter writes. "The thinking seemed to be that Zeferjahn was a potentially impactful enough addition that he could slot into a high-leverage role and stabilize the bullpen as a result."

Unfortunately for the Cubs, that thinking didn't materialize, as Zeferjahn has struggled mightily this season, enough to the point where Reuter called the entire bullpen a "ticking time bomb."

So, what has Zeferjahn done to receive such a bleak outlook? Well, in 11 outings for the Cubs this season, Zeferjahn has a brutal 7.20 ERA and -0.3 bWAR.

He's allowed eight earned runs and 13 hits, four walks, and two homers with 10 strikeouts in 10.0 innings pitched.

MORE: Cubs trade deadline addition Clay Holmes likely to opt out of $12M 2027 player option

His FIP of 5.20 does indicate he's not as bad as the 7.20 ERA indicates, but with a 1.700 WHIP, it's hard to ignore how bad Zeferjahn has been for the Cubs.

Considering his struggles, and how Daniel Palencia hasn't been good, and plenty of their other relievers are struggling, the bullpen might become a serious issue for the Cubs in October.

While the Cubs might've somewhat resolved the rotation, the bullpen is worrying. Hopefully Justin Steele and Edward Cabrera can return and provide quality outings out of the bullpen. Otherwise, the Zeferjahn trade only made things worse for the Cubs.

title: What Florida football's Jon Sumrall said at Week 1 SEC teleconference
description: Jon Sumrall spoke at his first-ever SEC teleconference on Wednesday about the state of Florida football ahead of his UF debut against FAU.
fullText:
Florida football's Jon Sumrall participated in the first SEC media teleconference of his nascent tenure as the Gators' head coach on Wednesday to discuss his team's season-opening matchup with the FAU Owls.

The new skipper was brief in his opening statement. "Our team, we had practice this morning," he noted. "We play Saturday at 7:55 against FAU and we're excited about it."

Sumrall went on to discuss topics such as his SEC head coaching debut, the quarterback room, offensive line coach Phil Trautwein, JACK Jayden Woods, the special teams and more.

Take a look below at everything Sumrall had to offer at the Week 1 SEC teleconference.

You gotta play with enthusiasm and passion, effort, and you wanna see them strain. You only get 12 regular season opportunities and you don't want to take any of them for granted, ever. And I'd like for us to play like we've practiced, you know? Look like we've done some things before and operate efficiently.

You see so many common mistakes that happen in Week 1 or Week 0 games like last week, and just for us to do what we've prepared in a crisp, clean manner is sort of the way you want to see it happen. But there will be guys making mistakes; when they do, I want to see them make them full speed. I want to see them go as hard as they can from the snap through the echo of the whistle.

Phil is really detailed. He's a great teacher. He's very consistent. Phil's a guy who doesn't get too high or too low, he shows up the same way every day. Like I said, consistency is a key there, I think. And I think just finding ways to help guys maximize who they are. Different guys receive things in different ways from a coaching standpoint, and so, how we reach each player is a little bit unique.

But he's very thorough with his preparation for his guys and I think he's done a great job. I did not shy away from — when we got here, I felt that the offensive line was an area that needed massive improvement. I think we've made improvements. Is it high enough for us to play the game at a level that we desire to? We're gonna find out real soon.

I'm gonna be pretty excited about it. I've said this a lot: I think back to when I was on the opposite sideline a couple times here as a player and as a coach, and how unique and special I've always felt like the Swamp is. And the fanbase here is so electric and charged up that I'll be very similarly wired. That gameday opportunity here is unlike many out there. And so, I'll be amped up.

But at the end of the day too, it's really about focusing on us doing our job to the best of our ability and playing really good football. And so, you have to make sure that while you're emotionally charged up and you're hyped, that you don't forget that the main things that go on within the game aren't in the stands; it's in between the white lines, and how do we help put our guys in situations to be successful.

I appreciate the shout-out to Ronny Massey. What a great man. You know, I feel appreciation every day I walk into our building. We've got the Gator head logo above our main entrance, and every time I walk in our building, I get excited about being here. And I don't take any day at the office for granted.

But, you know, to your point, growing up, I really idolized SEC football. I would watch every SEC game that was on TV or listen to a bunch of them on the radio as a kid, and to be able to have the privilege of leading an SEC team as a head coach is something I've dreamed about my entire coaching career. And, for me, it's the opportunity of a lifetime, and I will never take it for granted and will always have great appreciation for the situation I'm in.

I'd say, if you asked me early April who was going to start for us, really wasn't much of a conversation, just because of the difference of how well Philo operated at the line of scrimmage and ran the offense. The beautiful thing is Philo's continued to grow and get better, but so has the room. Tramell has stepped up and made strides. Aidan Warner has been really consistent and steady when he's had opportunities present. Will Griffin is uber talented, the freshman we got from Tampa. And then, Aaron Williams is also in that room, does a great job adding value to our football team.

But the whole room is elevated, which has made it more competitive, which is good for everybody. You know, you don't want anybody to become the starter because there's not great depth in the room. You want one guy just to elevate a little bit above the others, and I've got a lot of confidence in everybody in that quarterback room, though, that when they have opportunities, they're going to be ready to go.

I think it is, but you never know until you play. I think in preparation our urgency has improved. I think what you find out on Saturday is what your level of detail and doing your job at an elite level against another team, and it's not maybe in a practice environment against maybe people you play against every day. There's going to be some adversity hit in every game at every point all year. That's the biggest thing you can't really fully prepare for.

We simulate a lot of things to try and create what that looks like around our building and practices all the time. But there's nothing like it happening in a live game. We'll see what our urgency looks like against another opponent here shortly. I look forward to seeing how we respond to a lot of different situations that come up within games.

We've got Patrick Durkin as our starting field goal kicker. He was 25 of 28 last year and had a handful of them, I think four over 50 yards. So he's steady. He's got real ability. Yesterday on kickoffs, he was hitting most of them, eight, nine deep in the end zone, so he's got high touchback capability.

Alec Clark is our punter who's been starting punter in college football now for a couple of years. He's really efficient, catch-to-kick. He's usually fast getting the ball off and really is a consistent punter in regards to distance and hang. I like how he does things. The other thing that Alec does at an elite level is he handles the short snaps really well on field goal and extra points. He's as good of a holder as I've ever been around, which probably doesn't get talked about enough.

Snapping-wise, Carter Milliron will handle our long snaps on punt. He's played a lot of college football as a fifth-year senior. Then Lincoln Anderson is going to handle our short snaps, who is a true freshman from Hoover, Alabama, but has done a really good job this entire training camp and really shown that he is ready for this moment. Look forward to watching him perform, so those are our main specialists that will start and go on Saturday.

My first impression was positive, and it's only become more positive after that. He's a guy; when we got here, he was a high priority for us to retain. Then he made the decision to enter the transfer portal to just test the waters and see what was out there. We were able to hold on and get him to stay at the University of Florida, and I was pretty excited when that happened.

I'm even more excited about the fact that he made the decision to stay each and every day that I get to work with him. He's really, really talented. But more so than just being talented, he's as good of a human you could ever want to be around. He works at a really high level. He's very detailed. He's got great pride in his craft, and he's a high-character guy. I think the sky is the limit for what Jayden can achieve on the field.

But what makes it fun working with him day in, day out is just — holistically, he's a fantastic person. He has high standards for himself in every area of his life and not just football. He's going to be successful in any endeavor he takes on just because of the way he's wired. So very grateful he's on our football team. Like I said, I was excited off my first impression that we got to keep him. I'm even more excited now.

title: Payton Wilson takes jab at previous Steelers coaching staff
description: The Steelers linebacker
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers defense will look much different in 2026. Pittsburgh's defensive unit was the highest-paid defense in the entire league in 2025, but finished 26th in total defense. Under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham and key additions like Jamel Dean and Jaquan Brisker, there is plenty of reason to be optimistic about the direction of the Steelers defense this season.

Some players like third-year linebacker Payton Wilson believe that the new defense will allow him to play more freely. During his appearance on Cam Heyward's "Not Just Football" Podcast, the Steelers linebacker did not mince words when talking about the shift in his mentality this season.

"We were really tight as a linebacker unit, and they kind of empowered me in a sense to just go to play," Wilson said. "And then just [Patrick Graham], his schematics, the way he coaches it. I'm finally just getting back to playing ball, rather than 'Hey, if you make a mistake they might take you out.' Or 'Hey, if you do this wrong, you might come out of the game,' and you don't know when you're coming back. Not to say I'm going to make mistakes all the time, but now it's just playing ball and it kind of feels like my last few years of college again. It's slowed down a lot and I'm just excited to be back out there rather than I guess nervous, not nervous but just anxious."

Without explicitly saying it, Wilson seems to be calling out Teryl Austin and Mike Tomlin's coaching during his first several years in the league. It sounds like Wilson won't be nitpicked for his mistakes as much this season and will be able to learn on the fly, something that he is suggesting may not have been possible under the former regime.

Wilson totaled 79 tackles and nabbing an interception in his second year in the league. The Steelers' inside linebacker room will look largely the same in 2026, allowing Wilson to continue to grow as a key piece of the Pittsburgh defense and into a more confident player overall.

title: Golfer born with no hands relishes Pro-Am experience
description: Jersey golfer Adam Dalton describes playing in the British Masters Pro-Am as the "best trip" of his life.
fullText:
A Jersey teenager born with a congenital limb deficiency has described taking part in the British Masters Pro-Am golf tournament as the "best trip" of his life.

Adam Dalton, who lives by the motto 'no hands, no limits', has underdeveloped arms, no hands and only the use of his left leg.

On 26 August the 21-year-old took part in the celebrity event at the Belfry, Sutton Coldfield, which acts as a curtain-raiser for the four-day British Masters.

Dalton was teamed with professional golfers Hennie du Plessis and Marcus Armitage and finished in third place overall. He said the pair "were so lovely and really intrigued with my game".

Dalton first discovered golf while trying out many sports to see which he could enjoy playing without pain.

He found that it did not cause discomfort for his prosthetic leg, and has since the age of 16 been a member at the Royal Jersey Golf Club.

In July, he won the Cairns Cup, a disability golf tournament, as part of Team Europe, with the help of former Masters champion and European Ryder Cup captain Ian Woosnam.

"The difference between a professional hitting the ball and an amateur hitting it is awesome," Dalton told BBC Radio Jersey.

"Hennie and Marcus were so lovely and really intrigued with my game, which was cool.

"They were taking videos of me playing to show to their friends and team, so it has been a pretty surreal few days."

Dalton said it has capped off a "very, very big year" for his career.

"It's funny because we keep coming back from trips and saying that was the best trip I've ever had in my life, and everything keeps getting better and better, which is crazy to think of as possible."

His next stop is a competition in Italy, and then before the end of the year he will be heading to the Algarve region of Portugal for two more events.

title: How Carlos Narváez, ex-Red Sox prospects traded for Adley Rutschman are doing
description: Catcher Adley Rutschman will return to Baltimore on Thursday, one month after the Orioles traded him to the Red Sox.
fullText:
Catcher Adley Rutschman will return to Baltimore on Thursday, one month after the Orioles traded him to the Red Sox.

The Red Sox and Orioles will play a four-game series at Oriole Park at Camden Yards. Thursday's game is scheduled to start at 7:15 p.m. ET.

Baltimore selected the 28-year-old first overall in the 2019 draft. He appeared in 572 games for the O's from 2022-26.

The Red Sox traded three top-five organizational prospects — Anthony Eyanson, Kyson Witherspoon and Enddy Azocar — and catcher Carlos Narváez to land Rutschman on Aug. 3. They then completed the deal by sending No. 10 organizational prospect, Harold Rivas, to Baltimore on Aug. 12 as the player to be named later in the trade.

Rutschman has struggled with the Red Sox. He was acquired while on the 10-day injured list with left wrist inflammation. Since Boston activated him Aug. 11, he's 9 for 53 (.170) with a .254 on-base percentage, .245 slugging percentage and .499 OPS. He has one home run, one double, six walks and 15 strikeouts.

He has not played in the past three games and has missed five games overall since Aug. 24 due to a hyperextended right elbow injury.

Anthony Eyanson, RHP: The 2025 Red Sox third-round pick has continued his dominance with Double-A Chesapeake. He's 2-1 with a 2.14 ERA (21 innings, five earned runs), 1.14 WHIP, .208 opponents' batting average, 32 strikeouts and eight walks in four starts for Chesapeake.

The 21-year-old righty's best start was Aug. 20 against Richmond. He allowed just one run and struck out eight while recording 17 swings and misses in seven innings.

He induced 20 swings and misses in just 3 ⅔ scoreless innings against Harrisburg on Aug. 27.

Baseball America ranks Eyanson No. 34 on its Top 100 list.

Kyson Witherspoon, RHP: The 2025 Red Sox first-round pick is on High-A Frederick's 7-day injured list with a right shoulder impingement, according to The Baltimore Banner's Andy Kostka.

The 22-year-old right-hander made three starts for Frederick before getting injured. He allowed just two earned runs in 14 ⅓ innings (1.26 ERA). Opponents had just nine hits, all singles, and a .184 batting average against him. He struck out 20 and walked 10.

He tossed five scoreless and hitless innings while striking out eight in his final start against Wilmington on Aug. 21.

Carlos Narváez, C: The 27-year-old is 5 for 52 (.096) with a .203 on-base percentage, .115 slugging percentage and .318 OPS in 20 games for the Orioles. He has just one extra-base hit, a double. He has 19 strikeouts and four walks.

Enddy Azocar, CF: The 19-year-old is 30-for-90 (.333) with a .378 on-base percentage, .556 slugging percentage and .934 OPS in 22 games for High-A Frederick. He has three home runs, seven doubles, two triples, 19 RBIs, 20 runs, 18 strikeouts and six walks.

Between the Red Sox and Orioles' systems, he has 21 home runs, 34 doubles, eight triples and 82 RBIs in 106 games.

Harold Rivas, OF: Boston traded the 18-year-old outfield prospect as the player to be named later in the deal.

He played in the Florida Complex League for the Red Sox this year before being assigned to the FCL Orioles. The FCL is finished for the year but teams are playing Bridge League exhibition games right now.

description: TRACKER STATUS: SigningHouston Dynamo FC have acquired striker Lyle Foster on loan from EFL Championship side Burnley, the club announced Thursday.The 25-year-old South Afric...
fullText:
TRANSFER TRACKER STATUS: Signing

Houston Dynamo FC have acquired striker Lyle Foster on loan from EFL Championship side Burnley, the club announced Thursday.

The 25-year-old South African international's loan lasts through June 2027 and includes a purchase option.

He spent last season in the Premier League with Burnley, and represented his home country at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Foster joins Houston after they recently transferred Designated Player striker Ezequiel Ponce to LaLiga side Elche. Earlier this summer, they also acquired US international striker Duncan McGuire from Orlando City.

"Lyle presents another powerful, mobile forward to our attacking group," said president of soccer Pat Onstad. "He threatens the space behind the back line, links play well and brings the work rate and intensity that we demand without the ball.

"Lyle's experience in the Premier League and on the international stage will strengthen our group, and we are excited to welcome him to Houston as we prepare for a strong finish to the season."

Foster has tallied 30 goals and 23 assists in 194 professional appearances since breaking through at South African Premiership giants Orlando Pirates.

He's since traversed several European clubs, including Monaco (France), Cercle Brugge and Westerlo (Belgium), Vitória de Guimarães (Portugal) and Burnley (England).

Internationally, Foster has 10 goals in 28 caps with South Africa. He started their 2026 World Cup opener vs. Mexico and scored twice at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

Houston are second in the Western Conference (39 points), with winter signings Guilherme and Mateusz Bogusz leading the attack. The club's 30 goals are tied for the fewest among teams currently in the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs places.

title: Donovan won't 'underestimate' fired-up McKenna
description: Paddy Donovan insists he is not "underestimating" Tyrone McKenna before they meet at Croke Park on Saturday with a second crack at world honours on the horizon.
fullText:
Paddy Donovan insists he is not "underestimating" Tyrone McKenna before they meet at Croke Park on Saturday with a second crack at world honours on the horizon.

Donovan bounced back from his first title defeat by Lewis Crocker with an impressive victory over Karen Chukhadzhian in May to return to the mandatory slot for the IBF welterweight title held by Australia's Liam Paro.

The Limerick man is aware of the risks in taking a fight in the interim, but felt this was too good an opportunity to turn down and plans to put on a show to elevate his status.

He and McKenna have sparred countless rounds over the years and the 27-year-old, whose record is 15 wins with two defeats, feels he is a level above his fellow southpaw.

"It's risky to take the fight being number one with the IBF but I couldn't turn down the opportunity to fight in front of 80,000 Irish fans," Donovan said at Thursday's news conference.

"We want to bring big shows back to Ireland when Katie's gone and I'm going to be the guy to do it.

"I'm not underestimating you [McKenna], I've a job to do so I'll beat you and move onto becoming a world champion, but you're first and I'll deal with you good and proper."

'You couldn't make Taylor's story up' - Hearn

Taylor prepared for test rather than testimonial

'Dear Katie, how far we have come...' - Taylor gets reply from her hero

Veteran McKenna [25-6-1] has lost two of his last four fights after reversing a decision to retire following his own defeat by Crocker in 2023.

However, the Belfast man is not content to play the role of gatekeeper and set up camp in Philadelphia - where he spent an early part of his career - to work in 'The Dungeon' gym of Derrick 'Bozy' Ennis - father of undefeated two-division champion Jaron 'Boots'.

"To bring a west Belfast man to north Philly is a dangerous combination," said the 36-year-old.

"This is the most I've sparred in a camp, in a world-class gym surrounded by world champions and world-class fighters. The coaching has been world-class, so I've done everything for this fight.

"I think Paddy is overlooking me as all I hear is 'Liam Paro, Lewis Crocker', but you [Donovan] have to get your mind right because I'm coming for you."

Chief support on Saturday is a heavyweight contest between Dave Allen [27-9-2] and Thomas Carty [11-1].

Doncaster's Allen admits his ambitions of fighting for top honours are over following May's defeat by newly-crowned IBF heavyweight champion Filip Hrgovic.

However, he has bounced back with a pair of routine wins and feels he remains a "proper handful" at his level.

"After the Hrgovic fight, all of the feeling for boxing left me," the 34-year-old revealed.

"I'm not trying to resurrect any run for titles, I'm just here to fight but if you're not very good, I'll flatten you."

Carty once had aspirations to play Gaelic football for Dublin at Croke Park, but on Saturday he will realise something of a dream when boxing at the home of the Gaelic Athletic Association.

His sole defeat came at Madison Square Garden in March 2025 when suffering an ACL injury against Dajuan Calloway, but the 30-year-old southpaw feels he is "probably better now than what I was before" the injury.

Another Dubliner, Emmet Brennan, will make the 500-metre journey from his house to Croke Park to face fellow unbeaten super-middleweight Taylor Bevan with added incentive of double pay by Brian Peters, who represents Bevan, should he prevail.

Meanwhile, MMA convert Molly McCann continues her boxing journey against Sylwia Doligala.

McCann, who has won all four of her bouts since making the switch to professional boxing, is a relative of headliner Katie Taylor with her late grandmother a great-aunt of the Bray woman - and she recounted her own early struggles to find acceptance in the boxing world.

"I remember walking into a boxing gym and was turned away as I was a girl," said the 36-year-old Liverpudlian.

"[I] then started boxing at the Golden Gloves gym and my coach brought in a camcorder, told me to watch this girl and lo and behold, it was Katie.

"I was like 'oh my God, I want to be like that', and 20 years later here we are. It's not lost on me how many girls would kill to be in this position, so it's an honour and privilege."

title: Kyle Busch Classic Debuts Oct. 2 On The Bullring's New Pavement
description: Las Vegas Motor Speedway has done something short tracks almost never do for a driver who left them behind: it put his name on the calendar permanently. The Friday night program at The Bullring, the 3/8-mile paved oval inside the speedway grounds, is now the Kyle Busch Classic presented by Star Nursery. The first one runs Oct. 2, and it will run every fall from here. Busch died May 21 at 41.
fullText:
Las Vegas Motor Speedway has done something short tracks almost never do for a driver who left them behind: it put his name on the calendar permanently. The Friday night program at The Bullring, the 3/8-mile paved oval inside the speedway grounds, is now the Kyle Busch Classic presented by Star Nursery. The first one runs Oct. 2, and it will run every fall from here.

Busch died May 21 at 41. NASCAR's own account of his death noted his family's statement that severe pneumonia progressed into sepsis. He left behind 63 Cup wins, 102 in what is now the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series and 69 in Trucks, a national-series total no one else is close to.

This isn't a memorial lap and a moment of silence bolted onto someone else's race. The Bullring's event release lays out a full six-division program: ARCA Menards Series West for 151 laps, SPEARS CARS Tour Southwest Pro Late Models for 118, plus CARS Tour West Limited Late Models, Legends, Modifieds and INEX Bandoleros.

Why Robotaxi Hard-Braking Injuries Vanish From Federal Safety Data

Inside the Pagani Huayra 70: Transverse Manual V12 and a Missing Third Car

Those two headline distances are worth a second look. One-fifty-one and one-eighteen are strange numbers for a short-track feature. They stop being strange the moment you remember Busch ran the No. 51 truck for his own team and the No. 18 Toyota at Joe Gibbs Racing for fifteen seasons. Nobody at the track announced the math. They didn't need to.

The Legends feature runs 30 laps, and Brexton Busch is expected in it. That's the same class and the same distance as the Battle of the Busches father-son matchup at the Open Wheel Showdown in November 2025, which turned out to be the last time Kyle turned a competitive lap at his home track.

"Knowing his name will forever be part of the place that gave him his start is something I'll always cherish," Samantha Busch said in the announcement.

Here's the detail nobody outside the paddock is talking about. This will be the first circle-track race at The Bullring since Las Vegas Motor Speedway repaved it over the summer.

Fresh asphalt on a low-banked bullring does specific, predictable things. Grip goes up sharply, so lap times drop and old track records generally don't survive the weekend. Tire wear goes down, sometimes to almost nothing over a 30-lap run, and that's the part that bites. Falloff is what creates passing on a short track. When the right rear stops going away, the guy who qualified out front tends to stay there. Expect a single preferred groove until enough rubber gets laid down, and expect the second lane to be genuinely slower for most of the night.

For the teams, it means arriving with no usable notes. Every spring rate, shock setting and stagger number from earlier this season was developed on a surface that no longer exists. Crews will run stiffer setups than they're used to, because a high-grip surface loads the chassis harder and rolls more weight onto the right front. Anyone who guesses wrong in practice has a long evening. Anyone who guesses right can dominate.

If you're going, that's the thing to watch: who unloads fast on Friday afternoon, and whether anyone can make the top lane work by the ARCA feature.

The ARCA West field includes Vito Cancilla, making his series debut one day after his 15th birthday. That timing isn't a coincidence. ARCA's rule book sets 15 as the floor for competition, and drivers that age are limited to tracks a mile or shorter. A 3/8-mile oval is about as clean a fit as the ladder offers.

The irony writes itself. Busch signed with Jack Roush at 16 while still in high school, and NASCAR then raised its national-series minimum to 18, which killed the deal and parked him for two years. The regional and developmental ladders now handle what the national series won't, which is precisely why events like this one matter to anyone tracking where the next generation comes from.

Naming a race is a cheap gesture if the race doesn't sell. It becomes something else when the promoter has a reason to protect it. The Bullring entered 2026 under a new promotion team of Tim Huddleston and Kevin Harvick, with the fall date opening a 2026-27 season that runs through spring. Attaching a permanent, marketable name to the anchor event on that calendar gives everyone involved a commercial incentive to keep it healthy for decades.

What Camping World's Shrinking Store Count Really Means for RV Buyers

Truck Engine Fuel Rules Voided: What Federal Rollback Means for Diesels

The pricing reflects the grassroots intent. Adult tickets are $25 online or $30 at the gate, kids 12 and under get in free, and FloRacing carries it nationally. Compare that to what a Cup ticket costs two days later on the big track for the South Point 400. For a family already flying in for the weekend, Friday night at The Bullring is the cheapest three hours of racing on the schedule.

Gates open at 4 p.m., opening ceremonies at 5:30, green flag at 6:10.

Busch won more than 50 races on LVMS property as a teenager and took two Bullring track titles before anyone outside Nevada knew the name. In 2020 he came back and won again in a Super Late Model, 17 years after his previous Bullring victory. The track that made him now carries his name in return. Whether it means anything in ten years depends entirely on whether people keep showing up in October.

title: Barcelona already working on renewing three teenage breakout stars – report
description: FC Barcelona closed the summer transfer window on Tuesday with several new signings while also bidding goodbye to a number of players from the senior team as well as the youth setup.With the window no...
fullText:
FC Barcelona closed the summer transfer window on Tuesday with several new signings while also bidding goodbye to a number of players from the senior team as well as the youth setup.

With the window now closed, sporting director Deco now has a clear picture of the club's Financial Fair Play situation.

Now, the sporting department can turn its attention to another priority: securing the futures of several key young players.

Barcelona deliberately avoided opening renewal negotiations while the market was open, with the focus being on completing their transfer operations. That changes now.

Indeed, according to MARCA, the Catalans' immediate priority is to renew the contracts of three teenage starlets: Marc Bernal, Hamza Abdelkarim and Xavi Espart.

Barcelona have already made contact with Bernal's camp. Deco met the midfielder's agent in August, shortly after the club completed the signing of Rodri. The purpose of that meeting was twofold.

Firstly, Barça wanted to make it clear that Rodri's arrival would not halt Bernal's development. The club retain enormous confidence in the young midfielder.

New deal incoming for Bernal. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images)

Secondly, Deco used the meeting to present a proposal to improve and extend Bernal's contract.

Barcelona want to add two further years to Bernal's current contract, which runs until 2029. His financial terms would also be improved in recognition of his excellent performances.

The Blaugrana are keen to avoid any uncertainty over Bernal's future, given that numerous teams would be willing to pay a significant fee for a player of his quality and potential.

Meanwhile, Hamza Abdelkarim is another player whose contract Barcelona want to improve as soon as possible.

The Egyptian forward's development has been remarkable. At the end of last season, Barcelona exercised their permanent purchase option after the 18-year-old was included in Egypt's World Cup squad.

He made a number of appearances in the United States and impressed, before taking another step forward during pre-season with Barcelona, where he finished as the team's top scorer.

Barcelona want to increase Hamza's release clause. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images)

Abdelkarim's continued progress has made his current €15 million release clause look increasingly outdated.

Deco therefore plans to improve the striker's contract and increase the clause to €150 million, with a meeting already taking place with his agent earlier this week.

The third player in line for a new deal is Xavi Espart. The academy graduate was one of the standout performers of pre-season and has continued to impress during the opening matches, establishing himself at left-back.

Barcelona now want to reward his performances with improved terms. Espart's current contract runs until 2028, but the club do not want to wait before addressing his situation.

After his rapid emergence over the past few months, Barcelona are determined to ensure that one of their latest academy success stories remains firmly tied to the club.

title: Iraola confirms Barcola in line for Liverpool debut against Ipswich
description: Bradley Barcola could make his Liverpool debut within days of arriving, after Andoni Iraola gave a strong hint the winger will be involved against Ipswich Town.The France international completed his m...
fullText:
Bradley Barcola could make his Liverpool debut within days of arriving, after Andoni Iraola gave a strong hint the winger will be involved against Ipswich Town.

The France international completed his move from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday and has since trained twice with his new teammates.

Iraola addressed the signing at his press conference on Thursday, making no attempt to hide his satisfaction. "We are very happy with Bradley," he said. "It was our priority, let's say, to sign a very, very good player in that position."

He pointed to Barcola's attitude as much as his ability. "I think he has come also with the right mentality," Iraola said. "I've liked from him that he wanted Liverpool a lot. He just wanted to come here, and I think that's a good first sign."

The head coach also referenced Barcola's recent trophy haul with PSG, calling it evidence of the standards he can bring to the squad. "Being the player that he is and the things that he has won recently, I think he has come also with the willingness to help us," he said. "I'm very happy with him. He trained well with us."

Availability for Friday's trip to Portman Road looked close to confirmed. "If everything goes well in today's training also, he will definitely be available for tomorrow, yes," Iraola said.

Whether Barcola starts is a separate question, and one Iraola took time to consider before answering. "It's a good question, it's a good question," he said. "I see him in a good place. He has trained with us in three trainings. It's true that he hasn't had minutes in pre-season, but he has been training normal with the group. Then it's a decision we have to make."

He added a note of caution given Barcola's lack of match sharpness. "I think he's in a good place, but we also have to consider that he hasn't had the minutes in the pre-season games," Iraola said.

Barcola's arrival caps a £123m deal from Paris Saint-Germain, completed on the transfer deadline day and making him one of the most expensive signings in Liverpool's history. He last featured for France in their World Cup third-place play-off, and has not played a competitive minute since.

title: Brian Windhorst reveals why Kawhi Leonard was 'winner' of the Clippers' NBA penalties
description: Windy things Kawhi Leonard is a "humongous winner" after the NBA's Clippers penalties.
fullText:
Who won after the penalties were handed down by the NBA to the Los Angeles Clippers, their owner Steve Ballmer and Kawhi Leonard? The answer has to be Leonard, and that's exactly what ESPN's Brian Windhorst said on Thursday morning's Get Up!

Leonard will pay $700,00 in restitution for "improper benefits" for his uncle, Dennis Robertson... and that's it. The trade that will send him back to the Toronto Raptors sounds like it'll go through.

Here's what Windhorst said: "He's a humongous winner in this. He collected tens of millions of dollars in endorsement deals -- which are not permitted by the NBA -- and was fined $700,000 in restitution. It's the greatest investment you could ever make."

Brian Windhorst says Kawhi Leonard is a winner in all of this 

“He collected tens of millions of dollars in endorsement deals and was fined $700K in restitution. It’s the greatest investment you could ever make.”

(Via @GetUpESPN / h/t @TheNBABase ) pic.twitter.com/pWegv01Z13

Brian Windhorst speaks on how other teams reacted to the Kawhi Clippers investigation:

"There were some people who really felt like that the league should come down with a crushing blow, which is what they did. And there are other people who felt like a lot of the Clippers… pic.twitter.com/K5rhX0wOcA

"There were some people who really felt like, that the league should come down with a crushing blow, which is what they did. And there are other people who felt like a lot of the Clippers' penalty with Kawhi Leonard had been doled out over time, because this Kawhi Leonard arrangement was an absolute disaster for them."

"Adam Silver letting Kawhi Leonard getting away with this…Kawhi Leonard would be suspended for the year or he would pay that money back. The brother getting over $40 million a year, I'm getting that back if I'm the NBA!" - Stephen A. Smith pic.twitter.com/KD4NiVWM9I

Some consensus there between those two ESPN analysts.

title: Wisconsin–Notre Dame Ticket Prices Top Soft Week 1 Resale Market
description: Just two games have get-in prices over $100.
fullText:
Ticket prices for Week 1 college football games, which begin Thursday, are relatively soft at the top end of the market, with fewer must-see games than previous years' opening weekends.

Just two games have get-in prices over $100 as of Thursday morning, according to prices listed by teams' official ticketing or secondary market partners: Wisconsin–Notre Dame ($170) and Clemson-LSU ($110).

The Badgers are taking on the Fighting Irish at Lambeau Field in Green Bay on Sunday as part of the annual Shamrock Series that rotates among iconic venues away from South Bend. Meanwhile, Lane Kiffin is making his LSU head coaching debut in Baton Rouge on Saturday night with controversy surrounding the Tigers potentially playing former NFL players.

Here are the five most expensive get-in prices during Week 1 of the college football season:

Washington State–Washington: $88

Georgia Tech's matchup against Colorado is the Yellow Jackets' second-most expensive home game of the season—topped only by next week's visit from Tennessee ($114)—as Deion Sanders begins his fourth season as head coach of the Buffaloes. Colorado–Georgia Tech is on ESPN in primetime Thursday night, but overall Colorado is seeing less demand than previous seasons from college football broadcasters looking to put Coach Prime in the spotlight.

Auburn decided last year to move its 2026 home opener against Baylor to Atlanta as part of a multimillion-dollar deal that will see Tigers players receive NIL (name, image, and likeness) opportunities tied to the game's ticket sales and surrounding events.

While Week 1 ticket prices are not out of this world, Week 2 will be a different story as No. 1 Ohio State visits No. 5 Texas in what could be the most expensive game of the college football season. The get-in price for next Saturday's sold-out matchup in Austin is currently $528.

Last year's opening-weekend Texas–Ohio State matchup in Columbus had a get-in price of more than $330 in the day leading up to the game, which became the most-watched Week 1 college football game on record, as Fox averaged 16.62 million viewers.

Other pricey games in Week 1 last year included LSU-Clemson ($250) and Miami–Notre Dame ($200). Even TCU–UNC topped $120, as Bill Belichick made his head coaching debut in Chapel Hill.
