title: Terror for Rams fans with a devastating playoff forecast
description: NFL analyst Pete Prisco predicts division-rival Seattle Seahawks will shatter the Los Angeles Rams' season
fullText:
On Tuesday, NFL analyst Pete Prisco joins CBS Sports HQ to predict the playoffs and pick his Super Bowl winner. The Los Angeles Rams haven't even played a game yet, but bookies are already treating their playoff spot as a done deal. Bet365 has the Rams as the clear frontrunners to win the Super Bowl at +500 odds.

Prisco's playoff predictions show a different path for the Rams. He expects Sean McVay's squad to secure the NFC's top seed and a first-round bye, despite heavy title hype. According to his prediction, the 'dream team' Rams will get knocked out in their first playoff game by the division-rival Seattle Seahawks.

"The dream team... The dream team," Prisco said. "Yeah, we'll talk more about the dream team... Let's put it this way. The dream team ain't having good dreams. They're nightmares right now."

The Seahawks will travel to Los Angeles and physically bully the Rams out of the playoffs.

"I think Seattle would go in there and physically give them a beating, and it's going to be a... Look, they're going to be close games all year long when they play. This one's going to be no different. I think Seattle goes in and wins the game."

The analyst warns that when everyone hypes a team up, reality rarely matches expectations.

"They can win it," he said. "Look, any of the teams are available late in the playoffs that can win it, but I'm just concerned because it doesn't happen all the time and everybody's all over the Rams, so things might not go exactly how they think."

Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the NFL Preseason 2025 game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 23, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio.

Heading into 2026, the LA holds the league's top Super Bowl odds with a roster that looks absolutely unstoppable on paper. The Rams shook up the entire league this offseason by trading for superstar defender Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns.

Aaron Donald coming out of retirement makes this historically stacked Rams roster even more terrifying. They completely rebuilt their defense into a powerhouse by landing Donald, Garrett, Trent McDuffie, and Jaylen Watson. Plus, they are bringing back all 11 starters from last year's top-ranked offense, including MVP Matthew Stafford.

The Rams are heavily expected to take home the Lombardi Trophy this year. It is Super Bowl or bust for this team, anything else is a massive failure. If three-time Pro Bowler Stafford stays healthy, this team is a lock for a deep championship run.

title: Clemson Football Recruiting Needs in the Class of 2027: Defense
description: Earlier this week we took at how the offensive side Clemson’s roster is positioned for the class of 2027 and any portal activity. Below is a deep dive of the defensive side of the ball. It is amazing how much calmer things are when you come into the season with a full class of commits […]
fullText:
Earlier this week we took at how the offensive side Clemson's roster is positioned for the class of 2027 and any portal activity. Below is a deep dive of the defensive side of the ball. It is amazing how much calmer things are when you come into the season with a full class of commits and room to play with in the transfer portal.

As a reminder, the recent NCAA eligibility change means players have 5 years to play 5 seasons. Redshirting, etc. isn't the thing it used to be. A freshman is in their first year on campus, sophomore second year, etc. with the final year being denoted as a 5th year player. When we project future needs it helps add certainty in an era of chaos

DT: 11 (3 Fifth Year, 1 Senior, 4 Junior, 2 Sophomore, 1 Freshman)

With two commits coming in, DT looks well positioned on numbers. 10 DTs assuming no additional departures is a good spot. Transfers here would be a function of unexpected departures or the need to improve the quality of the position, it all depends on how the seasons ends.

DE: 10 (3 Fifth Year, 1 Senior, 1 Junior, 2 Sophomore, 3 Freshman)

Uncharacteristically, both DE and DT numbers look good. Normally one of the positions is a concern, but this year and for 2027 things are looking up. Sadly the talent may not be there like 2015-2019, but that will allow the staff to focus on quality transfers or key difference makers on the recruiting trail.

LB: 8 (2 Fifth Year, 3 Junior, 1 Sophomore, 2 Freshman)

With how poor the linebacker position has been, this could be a position with a lot of change. depending on how the season goes. But like other positions transfer will be able the quality of play vs. trying to flesh out the numbers.

CB: 8 (2 Fifth Year, 1 Senior, 2 Junior, 1 Sophomore, 2 Freshman)

Once again, the numbers seem pretty good here. You could quibble and want another CB or two, the two commits mean that Clemson will remain at 8 CBs, but depending on who gets classified as a safety, CB, or even LB it is hard to get worked up about 1-2 additional spots.

S: 9 (2 Fifth Year, 2 Senior, 3 Junior, 1 Sophomore, 1 Freshman)

Nothing much to see here, a theme on defense. Transfers and the desire to improve the team's talent level are really all we need to be worried about. Three commits with 2 definitely departing makes the safety room solid numbers wise

ST: 4 (2 Fifth Year, 1 Junior, 1 Freshman)

I just want us to kick the ball straight, don't care about anything else here.

Clemson is in a strong position across the entire roster for 2027. A full class of 2027 coupled with a good spread of players across classes will allow the Dabo to focus on critical needs in the portal. Either areas where guys left unexpectedly or the next man up isn't developing the way you would expect.

title: Who will USA play in 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup group phase? Full schedule
description: Team USA seeks a fifth straight gold medal with a roster featuring nine first-time players and veteran Breanna Stewart.
fullText:
The U.S. women's national basketball team hasn't lost a FIBA World Cup game since September 2006, a dominant stretch that has resulted in four consecutive World Cup gold medals. The Americans are vying for their fifth consecutive gold in Berlin, Germany, with a team mix of veteran and newbies.

Team USA is headlined by veteran Breanna Stewart, a three-time Olympic gold medalist and three-time World Cup gold medalist that'll join Sue Bird (5) and Diana Taurasi (4) as the only American women to appear in at least four World Cups. Aside from Stewart, only Kahleah Copper and Chelsea Gray have previously competed in red, white and blue at the World Cup. Everyone else is a newcomer.

"We have nine first-time players in the World Cup, so only three of our players have ever played in a World Cup before," Team USA head coach Kara Lawson said on Tuesday, Sept. 1. "There's a lot of newness to our roster... What is my message to the young players? Be yourself. Your play and your confidence is what brought you here."

Aliyah Boston, Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark, Napheesa Collier, Rhyne Howard, Angel Reese, Jackie Young, Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron are set to make their FIBA World Cup debuts. Here's who the USA will face in 2026 FIBA women's World Cup group phase:

The U.S. women's national team is in Group D at the 2026 FIBA World Cup alongside China, Italy, Czechia.

Group A: Germany, Spain, Japan, Mali

Group B: France, Nigeria, Korea, Hungary

Group C: Australia, Belgium, Puerto Rico, Turkey

Group D: USA, China, Italy, Czechia

title: Claudio Echeverri leaves Man City on loan to join Marco Silva’s Benfica
description: Marco Silva has another new addition to his Benfica squad, with the Portuguese club announcing the season-long loan signing of Argentine attacking midfielder Claudio Echeverri from Manchester City.The...
fullText:
Marco Silva has another new addition to his Benfica squad, with the Portuguese club announcing the season-long loan signing of Argentine attacking midfielder Claudio Echeverri from Manchester City.

The 20-year-old joins for the current campaign, with reports suggesting City will cover his full wages. Benfica are also believed to have an option to make the transfer permanent next summer.

Echeverri moved to City from River Plate in 2024 for €18.5 million, having been regarded as one of the brightest young talents in South America. However, opportunities in the first team have been limited, with the youngster spending time on loan at River Plate, Bayer Leverkusen and Girona.

An attacking midfielder by trade, Echeverri can operate centrally or drift into wider areas, particularly from the left. He made his City first-team debut in the 2025 FA Cup final and also scored a superb free-kick against Al Ain during the Club World Cup.

title: Cherki up for EA Sports Player of the Month award
description: Rayan Cherki has been nominated for the August EA Sports Player of the Month for August.The City playmaker got his campaign off and by coming off the bench against Bournemouth and providing two assist...
fullText:
Rayan Cherki has been nominated for the August EA Sports Player of the Month for August.

The France international was also at his brilliant best in the 4-1 win over Crystal Palace, scoring two wonderful second-half goals .

title: How Arsenal responded to Chelsea summer transfer interest
description: Arsenal’s upcoming opponents Chelsea showed interest in Martin Zubimendi over the summer, but the Gunners took a hardline stance against a sale.Photo by Julian Finney/Getty ImagesWith Manchester Cit...
fullText:
With Manchester City pushing to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea on transfer deadline day, the west London club went shopping for potential replacements.

Ben Jacobs reported for talkSPORT that Martin Zubimendi was among Chelsea's targets, but their interest didn't get them very far.

Gary Jacob reported for The Times that Arsenal intended to reject any Chelsea approach for Zubimendi, citing Mikel Arteta's recent insistence that the midfielder wouldn't leave.

Jacob confirmed in his report that Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso greatly admires Zubimendi, and that he also would have liked to sign the Arsenal midfielder when he was Real Madrid manager.

But Arsenal already had a deal in place at that time, and they had no interest in selling this time around.

It's not hard to see why Chelsea would be interested in Zubimendi. Other than Alonso's personal admiration, it was clear the Blues were after a top midfielder in Enzo's absence, and Zubimendi had just featured in all 38 games of Arsenal's Premier League-winning season in 2025/26.

Chelsea got to witness Zubimendi's talents first-hand during that campaign, as he started all four games for the Gunners against their London rivals.

Arsenal won three, drawing the fourth, and Zubimendi scored an excellent goal at Stamford Bridge in the League Cup semi-final.

Arsenal have also added to their midfield options in recent months, with Myles Lewis-Skelly moving back into a midfield role, and Bruno Guimaraes joining from Newcastle United. Perhaps there was a sense Zubimendi might become available late in the window.

But the Spain international has featured in all three of Arsenal's games so far, despite his late return to pre-season after the World Cup.

Arteta clearly still plans to use the 27-year-old this season, so Arsenal didn't entertain any offers.

title: Man United academy graduate tipped for surprise Dundee United switch after Eredivisie stint

fullText:
Zidane Iqbal is tipped to leave Eredivisie side FC Utrecht.

On Tuesday, ahead of the transfer deadline, the Manchester United academy graduate was expected to sign for Blackburn Rovers.

However, the Championship side could not get the paperwork and agreement finalised before the close of the English transfer window.

While it felt like he would stay at Stadion Galgenwaard, an interesting update has since dropped.

"Zidane Iqbal looks like he will be on the move from FC Utrecht. Dundee United a potential destination for the Man United academy graduate."

If Dundee United are indeed keen on Iqbal, as Peach suggests, they better move quickly, given the Scottish summer transfer window closes in just hours.

Iqbal is an elegant, press-resistant technical midfielder who excels as a deep-lying playmaker.

Unfortunately, he never got his chance at Old Trafford, and it is equally unfortunate that he never became a big hit at Utrecht.

A fresh environment like Dundee United, however, could give him the reset he needs to kick on and live up to his potential.

Iqbal is keen to emulate his idol Frenkie de Jong, and he may finally get the chance to do so in the Scottish league, should his transfer go through.

With a 40 per cent sell-on clause agreed with Utrecht, INEOS will surely be keeping a close eye on whatever deal is struck to take Iqbal out of the Eredivisie.

title: Will Southern Miss football win season opener against Alcorn State? Our prediction
description: View our score prediction for Southern Miss football's Week 1 game against Alcorn State.
fullText:
Southern Miss football has never lost to Alcorn State and will look to continue that trend in its 2026 season opener.

The Golden Eagles are hosting the Braves (1-0) at Renasant Stadium on Sept. 5 (4 p.m. CT, ESPN+). Southern Miss is 4-0 against Alcorn State and won the most recent matchup 40-14 in 2023.

This year's meeting will serve as Blake Anderson's first regular-season game as coach of the Golden Eagles. He was promoted from offensive coordinator after Charles Huff was hired by Memphis. His first game was the New Orleans Bowl loss to Western Kentucky.

Here's the Hattiesburg American's prediction for how the game will go.

Southern Miss is still working to find its identity after dealing with significant roster turnover. The team features over 70 new players and only two returning starters.

"For us, this game is really so much about figuring out who the heck we are at this point," Anderson said.

Many of the transfer additions were productive at lower levels such as junior college or Division II, and it remains to be seen how that will translate against better opponents.

The Golden Eagles are the clear favorite, but they are not sleeping on the Braves. Alcorn State went 5-7 in 2025, but finished the season winning five of its final seven games. The Braves were picked to finish third in the Southwestern Athletic Conference preseason poll.

"I told our guys very clear that this is a team that is more than capable of beating you here at home," Anderson said. "You've got to be ready to respect the opponent and I think our guys are doing that."

Why Southern Miss has an advantage: The Golden Eagles' offense has a chance to be explosive. Sophomore wide receiver Jaylen Himes led Division II with 1,174 receiving yards and caught 11 touchdowns for Wingate last season and was a standout during preseason practices. Himes, along with receivers Mario Sanders and Grant Page, can make big plays for the Golden Eagles.

Running back is another position that coaches were pleased with throughout the preseason. Senior running back Robert Briggs, who ran for 304 yards and a touchdown in 2025, will share starting duties with junior Steven Robinson, a transfer from Coffeyville Community College.

Why Alcorn State has an advantage: Alcorn State dual-threat quarterback Jaylon Tolbert is off to a blazing start. In the Braves' 56-7 win over Miles College, Tolbert completed 25-of-28 passes for 265 yards and five touchdowns. He also ran for 19 yards and a touchdown.

"Clearly, we're very aware that his legs are a problem," Anderson said. "We have to be both sound schematically and really good tacklers. It is clear if you give the guy space you're asking to get hurt."

Senior quarterback Ethan Hampton is back at practice after being sidelined for multiple weeks with a bone bruise on his hand. Anderson still has not announced who will start between Hampton and senior Landry Lyddy, but it does look like Hampton will be healthy enough to play.

There is uncertainty surrounding the availability of senior receiver Davis Dalton. Dalton missed both scrimmages with a hamstring injury.

Southern Miss 38, Alcorn State 17: It may take some time for the Golden Eagles to get in a rhythm. The slow start will allow the Braves to keep it competitive in the first half but Southern Miss is the more talented team and has home-field advantage. It should be a Week 1 win for the Golden Eagles.

title: Bearden's Brad Taylor discusses coaching Furman's Seth Henry
description: Former Bearden High School football players return to Tennessee with Furman.
fullText:
No. 18 Tennessee will open its 2026 football season Saturday when it hosts Furman (1-0).

Kickoff between the Vols and Paladins is slated for 3:30 p.m. EDT at Neyland Stadium. The contest can be watched on SEC Network+.

Furman has two players on its 2026 roster who played at Bearden High School in Knoxville, Tennessee. Punter William Pendergrass and long snapper Seth Henry will return to East Tennessee Saturday.

Pendergrass, who redshirted last season, graduated from Bearden in 2025. He played for head coach Josh Jones.

Pendergrass was a punter and placekicker for the Bulldogs, earning Second-Team All-Region 2-5A honors. He was also a member of the league's all-academic team during his senior season in 2024.

Henry is a true freshman for the Paladins. He was a long snapper and defensive end at Bearden under Jones and head coach Brad Taylor.

Taylor, a former Bearden quarterback, began his second stint as head coach at his alma mater after the Bulldogs fired Jones following the 2024 season after members of the booster club improperly paid members of his coaching staff.

Taylor was head coach at Bearden from 2007-13. During his first tenure as head coach, he coached former Tennessee running back Devrin Young.

Following his first tenure at Bearden, he was offensive coordinator at South-Doyle High School (Knoxville, Tennessee) under head coach at former Vol Clark Duncan.

Taylor discussed Henry's work ethic during his senior season at Bearden with Vols Wire.

"Seth is just a hard worker and he's a great kid," Taylor said. "Seth is a great long snapper and he worked at it. He didn't just do what was required.

"Seth and his boys, the other specialists, did a lot of work on their own. They worked before practice and after practice. They worked in the winter and they worked in the spring. Seth is always positive. He always has a smile on his face. He's just a great kid to be around. After his senior year, he worked hard to get ready to go down to Furman."

Taylor was also head coach at Karns High School (Knoxville, Tennessee). He coached Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop.

title: National showdown between Columbus, St. Thomas Aquinas headlines Week 3
description: Week 3 has several high-profile games including Columbus at St. Thomas Aquinas, American Heritage at Chaminade-Madonna and Venice at Lakeland.
fullText:
Columbus stunned Las Vegas Bishop Gorman, the No. 2 team in the USA TODAY Super 25 national poll, in Week 2. But the Explorers didn't get much of a chance to celebrate and relax.

"It's not like you win a state title, go home, you sit on the couch for three or four days and soak it in," Columbus coach Dave Dunn said minutes after the 33-28 win over Bishop Gorman. "I'll be watching film on Aquinas either tonight or first thing tomorrow morning."

5-STAR: A'mir Sears validates claim, 'I'm the best player in the country"

Columbus, which went from being unranked to No. 6 in the national poll, travels to top-ranked St. Thomas Aquinas on Sept. 4.

It's got a real argument for biggest game in the nation, and certainly the state, in Week 3.

But it's hardly the only high profile game this week. The schedule includes American Heritage at Chaminade-Madonna, Venice at Lakeland and St. Frances (Maryland) at Vero Beach.

Here are the top games in Week 3:

This game has a legitimate argument as the biggest game in the nation this week. Columbus is trying to pull off a second consecutive upset of a national power. Including the Kickoff Classic, Aquinas' defense has not allowed a point in the first half this season.

Venice and Lakeland are meeting for the first time since 2023, when Lakeland won the Class 4M state championship. Venice's offense has once against been outstanding, averaging more than 50 points per game this season. Dreadnaughts quarterback Kelin Hendrix threw for 193 yards and two touchdowns in the season opener against Kathleen.

Recruiting matchup to watch: Venice 2028 WR Tyree Mannings Jr. vs. Lakeland 2027 DB Jordan Young (No. 53 top 100, Pitt commit)

St. Frances (Maryland) is coming to back to Florida for a second consecutive week. The Greyhounds outlasted DeLand 49-35 in Week 2. Vero Beach quarterback Champ Monds (Notre Dame commit) has been outstanding this season. He has accounted for 11 touchdowns (seven passing, four rushing) with no turnovers.

Recruiting matchup to watch: Vero Beach 2027 QB Champ Monds (No. 22 top 100) vs. St. Frances 2027 EDGE Anthony Sweeney (five-star recruit, Texas Tech commit)

Raines, the defending Class 3A state champion, faces a big test in Ed White's high-scoring offense. Raines jumped out to a 24-0 halftime lead against Baldwin in Week 2 and cruised to a 52-14 win. Ed White was off in Week 2. The Commanders toped Trinity Christian 42-40 in overtime in the season opener.

Recruiting matchup to watch: Raines 2028 ATH Zion Green vs. Ed White 2027 CB Jacquari Parks (Wake Forest commit)

Madison County has been dominant early, outscoring its first two opponents by a combined score of 72-6. Michael Pride rushed for 85 yards and two touchdowns and had 73 receiving yards and a score against Gadsden County in Week 2. Columbia quarterback Amari Green threw for 124 yards and two touchdowns in the Tigers 24-6 win over Lakewood last week.

Cardinal Mooney is looking to rebound from its 47-46 loss to Cardinal Newman in Week 2. Cougars senior running back Connail Jackson has rushed for 496 yards and five touchdowns this season. True North lost to Coconut Creek 33-32 last week. Running back Jermiane Green rushed for 114 yards and two scores in the loss.

title: Cowboys Headlines: What now for QB2 Sam Howell? Emmitt Smith accused in $2.5M fraud scheme
description: Joe Milton is back in Dallas with a new role. So how will Sam Howell adjust to his? Also, Emmitt Smith is named in a $2.5 million fraud scheme.
fullText:
After all the wringing of hands and gnashing of teeth from much of the team's vocal fanbase, the Cowboys are back to the same three quarterbacks they've had all summer long. Joe Milton has made his return to the Dallas practice squad despite reportedly drawing at least some interest from "most" NFL teams. While that means his development can continue, what does it all mean for Sam Howell? According to the 25-year-old, it's simply a matter of getting back to work and learning all he can as Prescott's main understudy.

The front office, meanwhile, is already stirring up drama about next offseason's inevitable George Pickens contract situation, and we're still talking about the Micah Parsons trade: will all the defensive staff changes and personnel moves made since then collectively add up to what the Cowboys lost when they shipped Parsons off? Meanwhile, Emmitt Smith is facing serious allegations of fraud, and CBS is strangely quiet in the wake of Tony Romo's promise to work his way back to the broadcast booth.

Checking in with a few of the Cowboys' upcoming opponents, the Rams will employ a bold travel strategy in their Week 1 trip to Australia, while the 49ers have already boarded the plane to take them to the other side of the world... with a couple of their biggest question marks present and accounted for. The Ravens look to lock up Lamar Jackson, and in his fourth season, Jayden Daniels is getting a crash course in one of the most basic QB functions there is... huddling with his offense.

Elsewhere in league headlines, the Raiders and Chiefs are closing in on opening day with news about their starting quarterbacks, and the NFL continues to scour the globe for their next international gameday destination. (Konnichiwa, Japan? Maybe.)

title: 'You couldn't make Taylor's story up' - Hearn
description: Promoter Eddie Hearn says "the whole story, you couldn't make it up", when speaking of Katie Taylor's journey.
fullText:
As promoter Eddie Hearn tries to quantify the impact Katie Taylor has made throughout her career, there is a smile and shake of the head as he says, "the whole story, you couldn't make it up".

On Saturday night, Taylor will make her final walk to the ring when she takes on Flora Pili at Croke Park, with the chance to become undisputed light-welterweight champion once again.

While Taylor entered professional boxing in 2016 with an Olympic gold medal, five world and seven European amateur titles to her name, there were no guarantees that star power could flourish in the paid code where women's boxing remained firmly in the shadows.

After agreeing to meet Taylor, her mother Bridget and manager Brian Peters, Hearn's interest was more than piqued.

"I went into that meeting, I would say 90% in my mind I wasn't going to do anything," said the Matchroom chairman.

"She's so fierce and the way she was talking, like the passion, the determination and she was telling me the story about the Olympics [pushing for women's boxing to be added to the programme for London 2012] and I was just like, 'this is unbelievable'. That was when we decided to headline her in November."

The decision to put Taylor on after Ohara Davies' victory over Andrea Scarpa that night at Wembley Arena was met with some scepticism from his father, Barry.

"He's like, 'oh, mate, no one's interested in the women's boxing' but he watched her debut and he was like, 'oh my God'.

"From there, the story's been unbelievable."

Taylor made around £6000 for that initial victory, "at the time in women's boxing, a lot of money" Hearn reflected, but that proved yet another obstacle Taylor was determined to overcome for female fighters.

Following a defence of the WBA and IBF light weight titles against Cindy Serrano - sister of great rival Amanda - at Boston's TD Garden in 2018, Taylor questioned why Tevin Farmer, who defended his IBF super-featherweight title against James Tennyson on the same card, made significantly more money.

"She said, 'do you think that's fair?', and I was like, 'no, but I just think that's the world and where we are right now'," Hearn recounted.

"She's like, 'well, how can I sell more tickets, how can more people be interested in me, how can more people want to tune in to watch me fight, yet he's making three times as much?'. I said, 'because he's a man and that's what you need to change'.

"Now she's making more than 99% of male fighters out there."

The three fights with Amanda Serrano, two at a sold-out Madison Square Garden and another on the Jake Paul-Mike Tyson card in Texas, have helped transform career earnings and raise the profile for women's boxing to heights many could not have envisaged.

While Taylor again pushed her promoter to seek a higher purse than the "incredible" offer made by Paul's MVP for that second meeting, Hearn accepts "she was right" and despite fighter and promoter not having a contract "for years and years", he can only conclude the Bray woman has been "incredible to work with".

The love and respect for the 40-year-old has been evident in the build-up to Saturday's last dance with contemporaries, former opponents and many more outside the boxing bubble lining up to show their appreciation for a career that has transformed the female fight game.

"Boxing is a really toxic world," Hearn accepts.

"There's always people who don't like people but there isn't one female fighter you could find that wouldn't go, 'she's incredible'.

"She's just so loved, there's no airs or graces. She's not there for the fame, she's not there for the money, it's purely her faith, the love of the sport and trying to set an example."

title: Will 'proper captain's performance' be springboard for Shankland?
description: Lawrence Shankland nets twice in Rangers' 2-1 success at Falkirk, making it back-to-back wins after a sticky start to the campaign for the new-look Ibrox side.
fullText:
Watch Falkirk v Rangers highlights

On a night where plenty of his team-mates were panicking, Lawrence Shankland was a figure of calm for Rangers in Falkirk.

His two goals were decisive for Derek McInnes' side, earning a second Scottish Premiership win of the season days after the captain's penalty delivered the first at Pittodrie.

In an error-strewn game that lacked quality, Shankland was the difference maker.

His first whistled into the roof of the net off his weaker left foot, while his second - again on his left - was passed into the bottom corner with the game on a knife edge.

Falkirk boss John McGlynn summed up the Scotland striker's impact.

"If Lawrence Shankland is in a navy blue jersey, we win the game tonight," he told BBC Scotland.

After being linked with a move to his boyhood club for years, Shankland finally signed for Rangers in May after netting 60 goals in his past three seasons at Hearts.

The winning goal came shortly after he had slid a low shot wide with the goal at his mercy.

Shankland brace at Falkirk gives Rangers back-to-back league wins

Aasgaard makes Anderlecht switch as Rangers reject Raskin bid

"I'm very pleased for Lawrence," said McInnes, who followed Shankland to Ibrox from Hearts in the summer.

"I thought his second goal was particularly good, considering he missed the chance that he would be kicking himself with. But, like all good strikers, the experience of Lawrence, the calmness of Lawrence, the quality comes up with a big moment."

Before successive wins in the past four days, Rangers had endured a slow start under McInnes, dropping points in both their opening league matches and being knocked out of Europe by little-known Czech side Jablonec.

Shankland too struggled in those early-season games, but he now appears to be replicating his best Tynecastle form.

He has three goals in his four Premiership games this term and his link-up play on Wednesday was also impressive, bringing the likes of Djeidi Gassama and Kim Min-Su into play.

No player on either side had more shots and only Gassama had more touches in the opposition box.

"I'm delighted for him because it's not been, like for all of us, the easiest of starts," McInnes added. "Obviously Lawrence would feel the weight of that a lot more than some others, just because of his background and how eager he is.

"A proper captain's performance out there tonight."

As well as Shankland's match-winning display, the other item of note from a Rangers perspective was the return to action of midfielder Nicolas Raskin.

The Belgian is one of the club's most valuable assets, an established international who impressed at the World Cup. And yet, he missed Rangers' past two matches amid speculation linking him with a move away from Glasgow.

His influence was sorely missed in the Czech Republic as Jablonec forced a penalty shootout which they ultimately won.

But he was back from the start against Falkirk - a surprise after Rangers knocked back a loan bid from Turkish outfit Besiktas earlier in the day.

Raskin was central to Shankland's opener, winning the ball back in his own half before starting the attack by going wide left, and McInnes hopes he will remain a Rangers player beyond Thursday's transfer deadline.

"I'm just glad I'm able to choose Nico tonight," McInnes said. "We can do with his experience in there. I thought he got better in the second half. Obviously delighted if we manage to hold onto him and it looks like we will."

On a busy day transfer-wise, Rangers also accepted a £1m loan offer from Anderlecht for Norway midfielder Thelo Aasgaard.

McInnes expressed his frustration at having to play games so close to the window closing.

"Obviously Nico's had an opportunity to go today, and it wasn't something he wanted or the club, I believe, entertained. It was hardly the ideal preparation," he said.

"I've been keen to utilise Nico, but there's been a lot going on for him. He's been training with us every day, and I think at times the team needs more experience.

"Even coming through from Ibrox at lunchtime today, at the hotel, I had Thelo behind me and Nico three rows behind me and I didn't know who was coming and who was going. It's far from ideal."

Rangers have already signed 12 players this summer in an extensive rebuild and one more is expected to come through the door in the form of Portland Timbers striker Kevin Kelsy.

"It seems to have been the longest window I can remember - so much going on," McInnes said.

"For us now, it will do everybody good if we can get the window shut and work with what we've got. Players always settle a wee bit more.

"We've made some good signings, very young as you can see at times, but I'm confident we've got good talent here that can give us lots of encouragement between now and January and then see where we are."

title: 'We've got to find a happy medium' - Dowson confident on Pollock deal
description: Northampton boss Phil Dowson says he is optimistic about extending Henry Pollock's contract despite agent demands for seven-figure annual wages.
fullText:
Northampton boss Phil Dowson says he is relaxed about boxing supremo Eddie Hearn's ambition to secure Saints star Henry Pollock a contract extension worth a million pound a year.

Hearn, who signed a deal to secure commercial deals for Pollock in April, told the Daily Telegraph, external earlier this year that 21-year-old is "a seven-figure player" who "cannot stay at this club on the money he's on".

Pollock's current contract is thought to be worth £150,000 a year and expires in summer 2027.

"Eddie Hearn has a job to do, and that is to promote his client and ask for more money for his client," said Dowson. "He's doing both of those very effectively."

"We've said we want to publicise and grow the game and he has the ability to do that.

"[Contract negotiations with Pollock] are going well. We are still pushing it through.

"People have gone straight to the million-pound remark, but the other thing Eddie Hearn said is that Henry wants to win stuff, to stay at Saints and to play with our group of players. He wants to win the World Cup.

"I embrace that. I am all for that. The appetite is for him to stay. Now, we've got to find a happy medium. We really want to keep him, he really wants to stay, and that's a great start."

All Prem clubs are restricted to a £6.4m salary cap, with another £1.4m available in credits to incentivise promoting club academy prospects, compensate for absence on England duty and cover injuries.

One player's wages can also sit outside the salary cap, an exemption that allows Bath to balance the books while also paying top earner Finn Russell a reported £1m a year.

However, despite Pollock's marketability, it is rare for clubs to use the 'marquee' slot on their wage bill for a back row.

Players moving between Prem clubs are also unable to be nominated as their new employers' excluded player until they have played for them for two seasons, restricting his ability to demand sky-high wages elsewhere in the league.

Despite winning two titles in the past three seasons and reaching the Champions Cup final in 2025, Northampton have kept a tight rein on pay.

The latest salary cap report, covering the 2024-25 season,, external showed they were only the sixth-highest spenders in the 10-team Prem.

Fly-half Fin Smith, who extended his own deal at Franklin's Gardens last year, jokingly backed up his team-mate's demands.

"I think he's worth it," said Smith.

"He told me to say that, but I think it's hard to put a value on a player like that.

"You probably can't answer how much he does for shirt sales and putting bums on seats and things like that.

"But, hopefully he doesn't get a million quid. I'll be a bit annoyed about that.

Smith also told Rugby Union Weekly that Pollock's trip to visit Hearn's yacht on the French Riveria this summer had provided fodder for the defending champions' group chat.

"We were booking flights for our pre-season tour in Sri Lanka and Dowse [director of rugby Phil Dowson] was saying, 'can we go on your private jet please, Pollock?'," said Smith.

"I think he could definitely go to another club and get close to a million pounds but knowing him, he's desperate to win more than anyone I've really come across. That is absolutely his priority.

"There's all these theatrics and stuff that go on off pitch, but he's more driven than most of the people I've come across."

Northampton begin their Prem title defence at home to big-spending Newcastle Red Bulls on Friday 25 September.

title: Olid promises 'brave' Man Utd with new-look style
description: New Manchester United manager Eva Olid has urged her players to be "brave" and have an "attacking mindset" this season.
fullText:
New Manchester United manager Eva Olid has urged her players to be "brave" and have an "attacking mindset" this season.

The Spaniard takes charge of her debut game in the Women's Super League on Friday when United travel to London City Lionesses for the season opener (19:00 BST).

Olid, who arrived from Hearts, has taken over from predecessor Marc Skinner after he stepped down this summer.

That change and a quieter transfer window than many supporters had hoped for, has led to doubts United can challenge for a top-three spot this season.

Responding to those writing United off, Olid said: "It's normal, no? It's normal to have people doubting. I have felt the support a lot of too.

"People that followed me in the last years with Hearts know I made something impossible possible, so I believe in what we are going to do.

"It's not something you get in weeks but I believe with a little time you get impossible things."

Olid's message to her players has been clear and she hopes, despite an underwhelming pre-season, they can step up on Friday.

"My ambition is attacking football. I focus the gameplans on how we can hurt the teams. All teams have weaknesses we can exploit," said Olid.

"This team will play the first match in the league and I want it to be as close [as possible] to what I want. The style of play is different to what we had last year.

"You can imagine it's not an easy task. What I did was put aside the principles of play that I thought was easier to change for the first match so we can compete.

"The club wanted to play attractive football and be brave. We know that can have risks but the club support me in that. They signed me for that."

No WSL experience but who is new Man Utd boss Olid?

Media Day Diaries: Inside Manchester United

Olid's arrival comes at a time when United fans' frustrations are at an all-time high.

Question marks have been hanging over the club about their ambitions for the women's team and the apparent lack of attention from owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Their budget is significantly smaller than that of WSL rivals Arsenal and Chelsea and an underwhelming transfer window has led to many questioning if United can compete at the top this season.

But Olid's appointment is an intriguing one and she brings a track record of success with her from her time at Hearts.

United are moving in a new direction, focusing on developing young players and building an attacking football identity.

Olid was keen to stress this in her first meeting with the English media and came across as an astute tactician.

Sources at the club describe her as "football obsessed" and believe her ruthless work ethic will set a good example to young players breaking through.

She has been reunited with her former assistant coach Gavin Beith and has already hinted about recruitment plans in January that suit her attacking style.

title: Argentine league to pause games to honour Messi
description: The Argentine football league will pay tribute to Lionel Messi's international career by pausing all their domestic matches in the 10th minute this weekend.
fullText:
The Argentine league will pay tribute to Lionel Messi after his retirement from international football by pausing all of their matches in the 10th minute this weekend for a minute of applause.

The 39-year-old, who wore the number 10 shirt for Argentina, announced his retirement from the national side on Monday.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner's final game for his country, who he captained to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022, was the 2026 World Cup final defeat by Spain in July.

"In tribute and homage to Lionel Messi's career with the Argentina national team, at the 10th minute of play in all matches the referees will stop the game and a general minute of applause will be held," the Argentine Football Association said.

"We look forward to seeing you on the fields - join us in this recognition!"

Messi, who is Argentina's appearances record holder with 207 caps, first retired from international football in 2016 before reversing his decision.

That followed a defeat by Chile in the Copa America final, in which he missed a penalty in the shootout as Argentina lost a fourth major final in nine years.

The former Barcelona forward went win the World Cup and two Copa America titles with Argentina, scoring a record 125 goals.

Messi made his international debut in 2005 as a 63rd-minute substitute in a 2-1 friendly win over Hungary.

Having moved to Barcelona's La Masia academy as a 13-year-old, Messi has never played senior club football in his native country.

He is the second-highest goalscorer in World Cup history, with 21, behind France's Kylian Mbappe (22), and second for goals in all internationals (125) behind his great rival, Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo (146).

In August, he said he was considering his future in football after the death of his father, Jorge, who died aged 68 following a long illness.

When he announced his retirement from international football, he said following his dad's death he was "even more convinced than before" that he was making the right decision.

He will continue to play in Major League Soccer with Inter Miami, where he has a contract that runs to the end of the 2028 season.

title: Alcaraz 'stays calm' in US Open fightback
description: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz fights back from a set down to reach the US Open third round on his injury comeback.
fullText:
Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz avoided the prospect of an early US Open exit by fighting back from a set down against Portugal's Jaime Faria.

Alcaraz, 23, needed time to find his rhythm in the second-round contest as he continues to make his comeback from a long-term wrist injury.

But the Spanish second seed asserted his authority to win 4-6 6-0 6-3 6-2 against world number 72 Faria in the New York night session.

Alcaraz fighting off two break points in the first game of the second set proved to be pivotal.

"It was a tough match for me. I felt great in the first set, but I didn't take time and that cost me," said the seven-time Grand Slam champion.

"After that I tried to be focused, stay calm and think the good things will happen."

Going into the final major of the season, everyone wondered how Alcaraz would fare in his first tournament since mid-April following an injury to his playing right wrist.

The latest evidence showed the two-time US Open winner is beginning to gather momentum.

Alcaraz said he was playing "normal" in a straight-set win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round and reiterated after beating Faria that he is not holding back on his forehand.

"I know once I step on the court, I've just got to go for it every time. I've got to feel normal," said Alcaraz.

"I have to hit like I was hitting before the injury. I'm feeling great. There is no reason to be afraid and not hitting normal."

Sabalenka earns 53-minute US Open win - but tension still shows

Boulter wins one game in 58-minute US Open defeat

Birds stop play but Medvedev flies into third round

After coming through his opening match with little fuss, the questions then turned to how Alcaraz would pull up physically two days later.

Sweeping aside 23-year-old Faria answered those emphatically, although Alcaraz knows the tests will get tougher if he is able to move further through the draw.

As well as the likelihood of facing opponents ranked much higher than Safiullin and Faria, it will be interesting to see how his body continues to react to playing more five-set matches in quick succession after such a long absence.

On whether he wished he had been quicker against Faria, Alcaraz said: "At the end, I realised that playing four sets was really good for me to test everything physically, to test my body, how I feel, and how I'm going to feel tomorrow after this match."

With his fierce rival Jannik Sinner missing from New York through injury, and 24-time major champion Novak Djokovic already out, Alcaraz might increasingly fancy his chances of going all the way in a draw which looks to be wide open.

Alcaraz's next challenge will be overcoming China's Wu Yibing, who is ranked 113th in the world, in the last 32.

Meanwhile, American 20th seed Tommy Paul - a potential opponent for Alcaraz in the fourth round - continued his progress with a 6-2 6-3 5-7 6-4 victory over Croatia's Dino Prizmic.

Paul goes on to face Kazakh 15th seed Alexander Bublik, who cruised past French veteran Adrian Mannarino in a 6-3 6-1 6-1 win.

Eighth seed Ben Shelton continued his own quest to become the first American men's champion since Andy Roddick in 2003 with a 6-3 5-7 7-6 (7-3) 7-5 victory over Poland's Hubert Hurkacz.

Two-time semi-finalist Frances Tiafoe, another home favourite, demonstrated his great form with a 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 7-5 win against Japan's Rei Sakamoto, while Argentina’s Mariano Navone backed up his stunning first-round knockout of Djokovic with a 3-6 6-3 6-4 7-6 (7-4) victory over 2021 Wimbledon runner-up Matteo Berrettini.

Spanish 12th seed Rafael Jodar was the biggest casualty in the men's draw on day four as he was beaten 6-2 6-1 6-1 by Chinese world number 124 Bu Yunchaokete.

title: 'Humble but ambitious' - the return of fallen giants Schalke
description: One of Germany's fallen giants, Schalke are back in the Bundesliga after a complicated few years.
fullText:
On matchday, even for friendlies, Gelsenkirchen pauses as locals turn their attention to Schalke's Veltins-Arena.

Everywhere you look, swathes of fans in blue and white are arriving by tram, on foot or by car.

In the team's first game back in the Bundesliga for three years, 6,000 away fans stayed after the final whistle to support the players despite a 3-0 defeat at Augsburg.

"It's a kind of religious feeling that people have towards Schalke," said Professor Frank Eckardt, who grew up in the Schalke-Nord area.

"It feels like people think, 'OK, we don't have anything else, but we have Schalke. It's our club.'

"If you go to graveyards, for example, you will find that people have Schalke on their graves in one way or the other. So it is really something deep.

"You can take everything from us, but you will never take Schalke from us. That's what they really believe."

Alvarez to Arsenal? Plus Muslić on Schalke

Listen to the More than the Score podcast

When Schalke fell to Bundesliga 2 for the first time in 21 years and insolvency looked a genuine possibility - because of massive debts brought on by rash spending, failure to qualify for Europe and Covid-19 - the only guarantee was the fans would remain.

Despite the threat against the club's existence, Schalke bounced back to the top flight straight away in 2022.

A year later they were in the second tier again, and that is where they would stay for the next three seasons, with the first two campaigns showing little hope for the future.

A 10th-placed finish was followed by an even more dismal 14th - only two places above a relegation play-off spot.

German football expert Mark Lovell said: "They suffered with the burden of expectation. They were expected to basically walk the league every season despite having huge financial problems.

"There's sympathy for Schalke, but they've been their own worst enemies by chasing success and extending themselves too far.

"They've been living beyond their means for many seasons. When you do suffer relegation something has to give, and they haven't been able to buy their way out.

"They had to live more to their needs and get rid of their best players, and then sort of start again with a real skeleton type operation."

After finishing 14th, new figures were brought in - including former Plymouth Argyle manager Miron Muslic - who helped build Schalke's promotion to the Bundesliga last year.

Robin Haack, who covers Schalke for local newspaper WAV, said: "He is the face of the Schalke promotion.

"He is the hero because his way of coaching is so powerful. He gave the people the belief back.

"Nobody knew him before. Some Austrian who was relegated to the third league in England - he must be bad.

"But he proved all the haters wrong in an incredible way. Fans love him like I've never experienced a coach has been loved before."

Muslic operates with a high-press style and has created a team that represent Gelsenkirchen's working-class nature with committment and effort.

"Muslic was the perfect match," said Haack.

If Muslic was the cover star, working behind the scenes was former director of football at Werder Bremen and Germany international Frank Baumann, who joined Schalke in June 2025.

Andreas Ernst, who also reports for WAV, said: "He had the whole club, but it lay on the ground.

"They said do whatever you want to do. But with no money. We have a bad team. But come here - a very great club.

"Frank Baumann did everything out of nothing."

Lovell said: "At Schalke right now there's some very intelligent football people behind the scenes.

"Frank Baumann's a real top football man, and just a decent person, which Schalke didn't have."

Baumann's most eye-catching signing was former Manchester City forward Edin Dzeko, who joined in January after a torrid spell in Italy with Fiorentina.

He has scored eight goals in 13 games, including two this season in Schalke's DFB Pokal cup win.

Muslic told BBC's Euro Leagues podcast: "I grew up in Austria, but I'm from Bosnia. And Edin Dzeko for us is Gary Lineker. He's our Johan Cruyff. He's our Franz Beckenbauer. He's just an idol.

"He's 40 years old, and he's still able to perform. That means he was super professional the last 25 years.

"That's why he's a role model and that's why he will also have his impact and he will leave also his fingerprints in this upcoming Bundesliga season."

With his experience at top-flight clubs across Europe, Dzeko's will also offer something invaluable to Muslic's team.

Schalke defender Christian Fuchs told BBC's More Than The Score podcast: "Where it's a player like this... there's so much respect towards him from his team-mates.

"It's so important to build a club culture, to hold players accountable, to keep them all in check.

"Even if it's a small piece in the bigger puzzle, there is so much value that you need to give to that.

"Dzeko plays an important part in growing stability in the club."

Dzeko had been established with every club he has played for, but for others they have had to rebuild their careers with Schalke.

Former Liverpool goalkeeper Loris Karius has questioned multiple times whether to end his career, but has managed to regain a starting spot and become a key figure in Muslic's team.

Muslic said: "He is the face of this new Schalke, the face of this new resilience, this new mindset.

"After tough years behind him, he found a new home. He found new trust - like so many other players from Schalke who had some rough moments in their careers.

"They found a safe heaven. And then it was just about, let's do this together and let's start from scratch and let's do it in our way."

Schalke will need to showcase this new mentality against champions Bayern Munich in their first home game of the season on Saturday, after the Augsburg defeat.

This match will not define Schalke's season. Neither will the fierce rivalry with Borussia Dortmund. Instead, it will be shaped by every game at the Veltins-Arena, which will be packed with 62,000 passionate fans.

Fuchs said: "I know Dortmund. They don't admit it, but I'm sure they miss Schalke.

"Schalke is just a club that in my eyes belong into the Bundesliga and I hope... we'll see them there for a very long time."

Many Schalke fans do not have high expectations this season, with some saying they simply need to avoid relegation.

Muslic said: "We know the glory of the past. But we know also the present and the future.

"We are very humble but ambitious. Right now it's all about playing another year in the Bundesliga."

title: 'Dear Katie, how far we have come...' - Taylor gets reply from her hero
description: Ireland's first female world champion writes a letter to Katie Taylor, 30 years after receiving one from her.
fullText:
Before Deirdre Gogarty became Ireland's first female world boxing champion in 1997, she had already inspired a young Irish girl.

A 10-year-old Katie Taylor wrote to her hero in 1996 saying she did not "see boxing for girls taking off here", adding "maybe one day they'll even let us box in the Olympics". As Taylor is set to retire on Saturday as one of Ireland's greatest sportspeople, Gogarty writes back to the 40-year-old...

As I prepare to come home to Ireland to watch you fight at Croke Park, I keep thinking about just how far we have come.

It has been 39 years since I first walked through the doors of a boxing gym in Drogheda and was finally allowed to train.

Back then, I was told women would never be accepted in boxing. That even if we were allowed to compete, nobody would want to watch.

There was a time when I would have given anything simply to be allowed into a ring. We fought in places with few spectators, little recognition, and almost no opportunities for women.

And now, tens of thousands of people will fill one of Ireland's most iconic sporting venues to watch two women box... wow!!!

What was once considered unacceptable has become something an entire nation celebrates.

Katie, what you have done for women's boxing goes far beyond championships, medals, and records.

You didn't simply succeed in the sport - you helped transform how the world sees it, so that another generation of girls never has to question whether they belong.

When I sit among that enormous crowd at Croke Park, I'll be thinking about all the women who fought when nobody was watching.

I'll be thinking about the girls who were told they couldn't and shouldn't.

And most of all, I'll be thinking about the young girls watching you who will never have to ask permission to dream.

With enormous pride and admiration,

Thank you for writing to me and sending me you profile. Sorry I couldn't get back to you sooner as I was doing school exams. I train two nights a week up in my da's club. My da is having his own show in January and he is looking for a fight for me.

I am fed up not being to get fights especially when I see the lads I spar winning championships. There is the European championships for women being held in Sweden in May and my da is trying to enter me into them.

There is an open championship being held in England in April and hopefully I'll be entering that as well. I will let you know how I get on. Sorry to hear your fight in January is looking doubtful (Paddy was telling us).

I hope you can get it on. Hopefully if you get a fight in Ireland, we will all come and see you. My brother Peter recently won the Leinster nine counties and is the reigning champion of the Wicklow/Wexford championship and is fighting in the finals of them again in January on my da's show.

It will be a tough one as his opponent is the All-Ireland champion. I can't see boxing for girls taking off over here in the near future. I can see why you had to go away to get fights.

Hopefully things will change over the next few years but maybe one day they'll even let us box in the Olympics. I hope everything goes well with your boxing career. You have achieved so much already, you have done us all proud. I wish you continued success.

(Tell Christy Martin I'm getting ready for her ha ha)

title: Queiroz returns as Ghana manager two months after stepping down
description: Carlos Queiroz is reappointed as head coach of Ghana's men's national team, two months after he appeared to step down following their exit from the World Cup.
fullText:
Carlos Queiroz has been reappointed as head coach of Ghana's men's national team.

The 73-year-old, who had two spells as assistant manager at Manchester United under Sir Alex Ferguson, took charge of the Black Stars in April and led the side to the last 32 at this year's Fifa World Cup, where they were beaten 1-0 by Colombia.

Queiroz appeared to announce his own departure on social media shortly after that defeat, but the Ghana Football Association (GFA) has decided to re-engage him for another spell in charge following internal discussions.

The GFA has not announced the length of his new deal but said he will prepare the team for "a successful new phase on the international stage".

"The GFA believes Queiroz's extensive international experience, technical expertise and knowledge of the Black Stars position him strongly to lead the team into this next chapter," a statement added.

Queiroz has previously led Iran, Portugal and Egypt at major tournaments and has had stints in charge of South Africa, Colombia and Qatar.

Further details on his mandate will be announced by the GFA in due course.

Queiroz will begin his second spell in charge of the West Africans with qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, which begin later this month.

The Black Stars are yet to announce the dates and venues for their first two fixtures in Group C, where they have been drawn alongside Ivory Coast, The Gambia and Somalia.

title: Brand sacks execs over ad showing woman pushed over
description: American brand Good Good sacks three senior executives following a backlash over an advert showing a woman being pushed to the ground.
fullText:
American golf brand Good Good has sacked two senior executives following backlash over an advert which showed a woman being pushed to the ground after reaching for a club.

The company, whose YouTube channel has 2.1m subscribers, said it had parted ways with chief executive Matt Kendrick and president Joe Flannery following the release last month of the advert created for golf club manufacturer Callaway.

Good Good vice-president of brand and marketing Jeffrey Lefkovits was sacked earlier this week.

Head of finance and operations at Good Good, Alex Puchala, said the dismissals on Wednesday were a "difficult day for the entire Good Good family".

Nahid Giga, a board member and investor in Good Good, has been installed as interim CEO.

The video drew widespread criticism and was accused of making light of violence against women.

Good Good and Callaway removed the advert and issued apologies.

Callaway ended its partnership with Good Good and said it was donating $1m (£736,000) to organisations working to prevent violence against women and support victims.

Good Good, whom Callaway has worked with since 2023, has stepped away from its sponsorship of a PGA Tour event in Austin, Texas, in November.

Good Good products have also been pulled from the shelves of several retailers.

The advert showed Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark rushing over to Alexis Miestowski - a professional golfer and regular content creator for Good Good - and pushing her to the ground before shouting: "Do not touch my new driver."

The brand, which has become one of the largest content creators in golf, launched its YouTube channel 2020. Regular clips include men and women competing in various golf challenges.

Good Good also creates made-for-TV shows as well as adverts for golf clothing and other merchandise.

Puchala said Good Good was "concouraged by the continued support" of its fans and said it is "focused on moving forward and building the next chapter of the company".

title: Italian Grand Prix declared heat-hazard race
description: The Italian Grand Prix is declared a heat-hazard race as high temperatures continue in the country following the summer heatwave.
fullText:
The Italian Grand Prix has been declared a heat-hazard race as high temperatures continue in the country following the summer heatwave.

A heat hazard is an official designation for an event where it is forecasted that temperatures will be more than 31C at some point during the race on Sunday.

The ambient temperatures around Monza, north-east of Milan, are expected to be in the mid-30C region all weekend.

They peaked at 36C on Wednesday afternoon near Milan's Linate airport.

The ruling means drivers can use a system that flows cooled liquid, such as glycol, through a system of pipes in a fireproof top worn under their overalls.

The cooling kit is not mandatory, but any driver who chooses not to use it has to carry 5kg of ballast in their car to ensure they do not have a competitive advantage.

How to follow Italian Grand Prix on the BBC

Italy is the second race this year to be declared a heat hazard. The first was Austria early in the summer heatwave.

Some drivers prefer not to use the cooling kit because of discomfort, and because there have been issues with the coolant running out before a grand prix is finished.

In that case, the liquid ends up at car temperature, which is considerably higher than ambient.

Temperatures in the cockpit of an F1 car can be more than 40C, and drivers are wearing several layers of fireproof clothing in addition to a balaclava and helmet, so overheating is a serious concern.

title: 'What kind of question is that?' - Sabalenka spiky after ruthless win
description: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka cruises into the US Open third round before a spiky exchange with a journalist.
fullText:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka earned one of the quickest Grand Slam wins of her career with a 53-minute pummelling of US Open debutant Polina Iatcenko in the second round.

However, the world number one did not look entirely happy even as she swept aside Iatcenko - then had a spiky exchange with a reporter in her post-match news conference.

Sabalenka took umbrage with what she perceived to be a suggestion from a reporter that she had been attending "lots of parties" in the build-up to the US Open.

"What kind of question is that? Just because I posted some activities with brands, you think that I've been partying [and] not training?" countered Sabalenka.

Asked if she was "getting serious" now the tournament was under way, she said: "Oh yeah, I wasn't serious before that. Next question."

Sabalenka, 28, is aiming to win her first major title of a strange season where she has enjoyed spectacular success but is now looking to recover from a recent dip.

Coasting to a 6-1 6-1 victory over 22-year-old qualifier Iatcenko did not offer a true test of where Sabalenka's level is.

But the ruthless manner in which she secured victory will certainly boost confidence as she looks to complete a rare 'three-peat' of US Open titles.

"I'm happy with the level I played, happy with the focus and happy to be through this match," said Sabalenka, who will play Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova in the third round.

Boulter wins one game in 58-minute US Open defeat

Birds stop play but Medvedev flies into third round

Sabalenka knows she must the lift the trophy in New York again to stand any chance of preventing Elena Rybakina taking her position at the top of the rankings.

Even if Sabalenka does retain the title, Rybakina would still rise to the summit by reaching the semi-finals.

Sabalenka losing the top spot seemed unthinkable after a storming start to the season, reaching the Australian Open final and winning the Indian Wells and Miami titles back-to-back.

Losing to Rybakina in Melbourne was Sabalenka's only defeat in her first 27 matches of 2026. After completing the Sunshine Double, her win-loss record leading into the US Open dropped to 17-7 and she has only reached one WTA semi-final in the past five months.

Before the final Grand Slam of the season, Sabalenka admitted she had been "dealing with several things" in a period which she knows was far below her best.

Sabalenka's pace and power was too much for world number 160 Iatcenko, who managed just three winners compared to the 24 put away by the top seed.

Iatcenko looked a bundle of nerves in the biggest match of her career, but composed herself to get on the scoreboard for 5-1 and immediately broke out into a relieved smile.

It was merely respite as Sabalenka held to love in fewer than 90 seconds to clinch the opening set.

Despite only being on court for 24 minutes, Iatchenko decided she wanted a bathroom break to change her kit - but more likely for a mental reset than anything else.

Sabalenka kept loose while she waited by practising her serves and maintained her rhythm as she surged a double break ahead for 3-0 in the second set.

It was not all plain-sailing for Sabalenka as she lost serve in a sloppy fourth game, but reasserted her authority with two more breaks as Iatchenko was taught a harsh lesson.

The Russian can console herself with the knowledge she has gained valuable experience against the world number one on the biggest court on the planet - and a bumper paycheck.

Coming into the US Open, she had earned $300,000 (£220,000) in her career but takes another $190,000 home from New York to reinvest into her future.

Earlier on Wednesday, third seed Pegula continued her quest for a maiden Grand Slam singles title with a comfortable victory over fellow American Sofia Kenin.

Pegula also has a shot of replacing Sabalenka as world number one if she wins the title, as does fourth seed Coco Gauff, and kept her dream alive with a 6-3 6-1 win.

There were also straight-set wins for Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, SW19 runner-up Karolina Muchova, two-time major semi-finalist Marta Kostyuk and teenage American sensation Iva Jovic as the pattern of few shocks in the women's draw over the opening two rounds continued.

title: Ashes ticket price increase 'really poor' - Vaughan
description: Former England captain Michael Vaughan is critical of a 43% ticket price increase for next year's men's Ashes Test at Edgbaston.
fullText:
Former England captain Michael Vaughan has called a 43% ticket price increase for next year's men's Ashes Test at Edgbaston "really poor".

The Birmingham ground will host the third Test of the best-of-five series between England and Australia next summer, with ticket prices in the Hollies Stand - which holds almost 6,000 spectators - costing £165, up from £115 in 2023.

Elsewhere in the stadium, members can purchase tickets for £92, but the cheapest adult tickets across the first three days are £115, with every ticket carrying a £2.50 booking fee.

"This is really poor," Vaughan posted on social media in response to the news.

Following the 2023 series, which ended in a 2-2 draw after Australia won the first two Tests (at Edgbaston and Lord's), the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) said "every day sold out in advance, with total attendance topping 545,000".

An Edgbaston Stadium spokesperson said: "Our prices for the 2027 Ashes Test are broadly in line with other host venues and major British sporting events such as Wimbledon and the Formula One at Silverstone.

"Our entry level ticket prices roughly match inflation compared to the last time Australia visited Edgbaston in 2023 - but like the rest of the country, we're battling increased costs and trying to manage these wherever we can."

Despite Warwickshire's Edgbaston stadium being at a reduced capacity because of the construction of an on-site hotel, tickets for next week's third Test between England and Pakistan, which range between £57.50-£87.50 for adults, have not sold out.

The ticket ballot for the 2027 Ashes opened on Wednesday, with prices more expensive at Lord's and the Oval in London, with the best tickets at £190 and £185.

England, who lost 4-1 in Australia last winter, begin their quest to regain the Ashes at Trent Bridge in Nottingham on 18 June.

The second Ashes Test at Lord's begins on 30 June and the third at Edgbaston on 8 July.

The Utilita Bowl in Southampton will become the 10th UK ground to host a men's Ashes Test when the fourth Test gets under way on 21 July, with the series concluding at the Kia Oval from 29 July.

BBC Sport has contacted the ECB and all the Test venues for comment.

Ticket prices for sporting events have been an ongoing point of contention for fans.

A crowd of 13,623 were at Birmingham's 23,000-capacity Alexander Stadium to watch Britain's 24-year-old sprinter Amy Hunt win the women's 100m at the European Athletics Championships last month.

Athletics supporters blamed ticket prices, with Category A tickets for the home straight costing £150.

For the men's 100m final those same seats cost £110, again with no concessions for juniors.

In April, Ryder Cup organisers defended ticket prices for next year's centenary golf event between Europe and the United States in Ireland.

Daily general admission tickets for the three tournament days on 17-19 September at Adare Manor in County Limerick will cost 499 euros (£434), compared with up to 260 euros in Italy in 2023.

title: Tifo, rollercoaster or both? Osnabruck unveil new display
description: VfL Osnabruck showcase a tifo that took months to plan before their German Cup tie against Bayern Munich.
fullText:
Whether it is Borussia Dortmund's famous 'Yellow Wall' or the displays that fill the stands of Bayern Munich's Allianz Arena, Germany has long perfected the art of the tifo.

But second division side VfL Osnabruck have surely topped anything previously seen at a German football match by creating a tifo featuring a rollercoaster.

Showcased before their 4-1 German Cup first-round defeat by Bayern Munich on Wednesday, the tifo displayed the words 'VfL Osnabruck – a rollercoaster ride!' and a wooden cart that went along the track at the Bremer Brucke stadium.

Osnabruck said the tifo symbolised its turbulent club history in a journey fans refer to as a "rollercoaster ride full of ups and downs".

After "several months" of planning and building, the display also featured some of the club's major triumphs like a 1978 victory over Bayern Munich and a number of "scandals and bitter defeats".

The rollercoaster structure in front of the East Stand was built from wooden slats, plastic piping, fabric and was designed to be rolled out in sections.

The cart, constructed primarily from wood and styrofoam, carried dummies and was repeatedly transported back to the starting point for a continuous ride through a push and pull system.

The fun doesn't end there though.

Osnabruck, who have recently been promoted to Bundesliga 2, said the cart passed a "photo station" where a flash went off and the "photo" of that cart instantly appeared on the right side of the grandstand.

Fans even recorded a special 'Funpark Bremer Brucke' song before the match to accompany the display.

The tifo was taken down just before kick-off, but the party-like atmosphere continued when Osnabruck took a shock 1-0 lead after just five minutes.

Bayern, the reigning German Cup and Bundesliga champions, had to rely on two goals from England captain Harry Kane, as well as goals from Tom Bischof and Michael Olise to reach the second round.
