title: North Korea ruling party revisions bolster Kim Jong Un's control, report says
description: North Korea's revision of rules governing the Workers' Party lays the groundwork for more centralised control under the reclusive state's leader Kim Jong Un, a
fullText:
SEOUL, Sept 3 (Reuters) - North Korea's revision of rules governing the Workers' Party lays the groundwork for more centralised control under ‌the reclusive state's leader Kim Jong Un, a South Korean security institute ‌report said on Thursday.

The revisions, adopted at the ruling Workers' Party of Korea's Ninth Congress in ​February, strengthened Kim's authority and further institutionalised party control over the state and military, said the Institute for National Security Strategy, which is affiliated with South Korea's National Intelligence Service.

The rules give the party's general secretary, a post held by ‌Kim, explicit powers to convene ⁠and chair Politburo and Politburo Standing Committee meetings, appoint and dismiss key officials, admit or expel party members, and dissolve party ⁠organisations and departments.

The provisions allow Kim to exercise more direct control without relying on collective party decision-making bodies, the report said.

Other changes were aimed at regularising party ​operations and ​tightening central oversight of government and military ​affairs.

The revised rules require Central ‌Committee plenary meetings at least once every six months. They also allow the Politburo, when authorised by the Central Committee, to decide major issues in wartime, a step intended to avoid delays by allowing a smaller group of senior officials to act without convening the full committee.

The report said the revisions removed ‌remaining references to the achievements of Kim's grandfather, ​state founder Kim Il Sung, and his father, ​former leader Kim Jong Il, ​while emphasising Kim Jong Un's central role.

The revised rules also ‌retained North Korea's abandonment of its ​longstanding unification policy toward ​South Korea, after Pyongyang deleted related language in 2024 under its "two hostile states" framework.

Other changes raised the minimum party membership age to 20 from ​18 and expanded disciplinary ‌measures against members.

The institute described the revisions as part of a "Kim ​Jong Un era 2.0", further consolidating authority around the North Korean ​leader.

title: Airline involved in low stadium flyover turns over black box data as investigators probe if safety rules were violated
description: The airline behind a remarkably low planned flyover of a packed rugby stadium said Wednesday it will turn over data from the planes’ black boxes to show the maneuver was done in accordance with govern...
fullText:
The airline behind a remarkably low planned flyover of a packed rugby stadium said Wednesday it will turn over data from the planes' black boxes to show the maneuver was done in accordance with governmental rules.

The two 98-seat Embraer-190 regional jets from South African airline Airlink buzzed Cape Town's DHL stadium on Saturday just before the match between the country's Springboks and New Zealand's All Blacks teams.

The planes' lowest altitude was only about 46 feet above the roof of the stadium, according to the tracking website Flightradar 24.

"The data recorded by both aircrafts' digital flight data recorders (black boxes) indicate that the flights were performed within the (South African Civil Aviation Authority's) approved and rehearsed safety altitude and speed limits for the fly-past," Airlink said in a statement to CNN on Wednesday.

The airline said authorities provided "guidance, approval and support to ensure a safe flyby," and each of the planes were flown by three senior captains, including one who acted as a safety/technical officer. No passengers were onboard.

The aviation authority is now examining the flight data and has requested additional information from Airlink, according to a statement posted online.

"It is therefore critical that we interrogate this past weekend's events with clear minds and data at our disposal to determine if there were any safety concerns which warrant a review," the agency said.

Airlink staged a similar flyby over Johannesburg's Ellis Park stadium one week earlier, using the same specially painted jets celebrating "rugby's greatest rivalry."

The airline withdrew an application for a third flyover planned for this coming weekend, the aviation authority said.

Many in South Africa, which the US has determined meets international standards for aviation oversight, have celebrated the flyover.

"It's a well known fact that we have the best pilots in the world, that was spectacular, next time I will ask the pilots to land on the field, prepare to be amazed further," the South African Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture Gayton McKenzie joked online shortly after the flyover.

"We are cooking something," he posted Wednesday standing in front of another Airlink jet.

Many aviation experts believe the flight was not worth the risk, with the extremely low altitude leaving no margin for error.

"It was a very unsafe procedure and not necessary," former NTSB chairman Pete Goelz told CNN. "A flyby at 1,000 ft is already impressive, and people enjoy it, and there's no reason to lower it other than unnecessary risk taking."

United States rules say a plane must remain at least a thousand feet above congested areas, unless it has explicit permission from the Federal Aviation Administration.

Low-flying airliners are, however, part of South African rugby history.

In 1995, a South African Airways Boeing 747 famously flew over the Rugby World Cup final in Johannesburg.

And in 2024, an Emirates A380 flew over the same stadium, though a few hundred feet higher.

Saturday's flyover in Cape Town punctuates a summer of aircraft flying stunningly close to the ground.

In July, a pilot from the U.S. Navy's Blue Angels flew low over the crowd during the Pensacola Beach air show, sending tents flying and military leaders scrambling to defend the maneuver.

A month before, a Boeing 777 on a test flight passed as low as 25 feet over a runway at Horseshoe Bay, Texas, triggering a federal investigation.

title: Mexican musician, pregnant wife, child and nanny killed in grisly shootings
description: A Mexican musician, his pregnant wife and 3-year-old daughter, as well as their nanny and a family dog were found dead on Tuesday, in a gruesome homicide case.
fullText:
EDITOR'S NOTE:  This story contains details some readers might find disturbing.

A Mexican musician, his pregnant wife and 3-year-old daughter, as well as their nanny and a family dog were found dead on Tuesday, in a gruesome homicide case.

Jonathan Meléndez, the 38-year-old keyboardist of the well-known indie rock band Camilo Séptimo, was among those found dead in an apartment in an upscale neighborhood near Mexico City late Tuesday night, the State of Mexico Attorney General's Office said. His wife, Ana Paula, 35, was four months pregnant.

The second woman's family confirmed to reporters that the 21-year-old, named Aleida Romero Victorio, worked for the couple as a nanny.

"She was a very hardworking and responsible girl who did not deserve for this to be done to her," said her aunt, Lorena Victorio Cabrera.

Three of the victims – including the young girl – were shot in the head, authorities said, while the other was shot in the back.

"Two of the victims were found with their hands bound," the prosecutor's office said. The dog was found dead, with its legs tied.

A 6-year-old boy was found alive at the scene and was unharmed, they added.

Authorities believe the killings occurred between 5:30 p.m. and 7:40 p.m. on Tuesday.

Meléndez's band said he would be remembered "with immense love and gratitude."

"Today we honor and celebrate his life, his music, his light, and what he shared with those of us fortunate enough to know him and walk alongside him," Camilo Séptimo said on Instagram.

Two men were arrested in connection with the deaths on Wednesday, in a joint operation involving the State of Mexico Prosecutor's Office, the federal Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection and the Mexico City Secretariat of Citizen Security.

An associate of Meléndez, identified as Diego Sebastián "N," is accused of being the probable perpetrator, the prosecutor's office said.

Another man identified as Gerardo "N" is also under investigation for his alleged involvement.

CNN is trying to determine if the detainees have legal representation.

One of the suspects allegedly "exploited" his relationship with one of the victims to enter the home, according to Omar García Harfuch, Mexico's secretary of security and citizen protection.

The prosecutor's office said it would disclose the circumstances of the killings and the legal status of the detainees at the appropriate procedural stage.

CNN's Michael Rios contributed to this report.

title: Democrats block proposed constitutional amendment to keep Supreme Court justices to nine
description: A Republican proposal to amend the Constitution to prevent expanding the number of justices on the Supreme Court failed on the House floor. Like all constitutional amendments, the measure needed a two...
fullText:
A Republican proposal to amend the Constitution to prevent expanding the number of justices on the Supreme Court failed on the House floor.

Like all constitutional amendments, the measure needed a two-thirds majority of the House to pass, which it did not get: The vote was along party lines at 212-206. Democrats have never supported such an amendment, so it will be easy fodder for Republicans to accuse Democrats of looking to "pack the court" with favorable liberal justices.

Rep. Brad Knott (R-N.C.), a member of the Judiciary Committee, said he wasn't surprised the vote was along party lines, even though Democrats, in his view, knew there would be "political risk" to voting no.

"Democrats are very clear. They want to pack the court," Knott said. "We want to maintain the normalcy and stick with the process that we've done for a long time."

The Republican campaign arm wasted no time spinning the vote into midterm messaging. Mike Marinella, a spokesperson for the National Republican Congressional Committee, which helps support and elect Republican candidates, wrote in a statement released minutes after the vote that Democrats voted against the amendment "so they can follow through on a radical socialist agenda."

"Give House Democrats an ounce of power, and they'll use every bit of it to fundamentally transform America into an unrecognizable socialist hellscape," Marinella said.

The Supreme Court issue is red meat for Republicans, who have been against "court packing" since the days of former President Franklin Roosevelt and are eager to jump on any controversial Democratic ideas as midterm ammo.

Democrats have floated the idea of adding justices to the court for years, especially when the current justices have ruled in favor of the Trump administration.

Most Democrats, including top leaders, dismissed the resolution, which was sponsored by Rep. Andy Biggs (R-Ariz.), as a campaign stunt designed solely to animate conservatives ahead of the midterms. They're confident that voters will care more about the cost of living, which has risen under Trump's second term, when they go to the polls.

"This is such a fake issue that Republicans are putting on," Rep. Pete Aguilar (Calif.), chair of the House Democratic Caucus, told reporters this week. "I understand why they're putting it on, [but] the American public aren't asking about this."

Aguilar said he traveled extensively over the long summer break and heard no concerns about the Supreme Court issue.

"Nowhere ever are people saying, 'You know what we should do? We should cap the number of Supreme Court justices,'" he said.

title: Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and wife seek to end drug charges case on immunity grounds
description: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife asked a judge on Wednesday to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment against them on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and firs...
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife asked a judge on Wednesday to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment against them on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country.

In papers filed in Manhattan federal court, lawyers for Maduro said a judge was required by law to reject the indictment because it cannot be brought against a foreign leader.

"No American court has ever presided over the criminal trial of a foreign leader who was recognized by their own country as the sitting head of state at the time the charges were brought," the lawyers wrote. "That is not an accident of history. It reflects a rule older than the common law: heads of state are exempt from the criminal process of any national court but their own."

Maduro and his wife are scheduled to go on trial on drug trafficking charges next June 1. Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein has set oral arguments for Nov. 17 on motions to dismiss the indictment.

Maduro, 63, and his wife, Cilia Flores, 69, have been held at a Brooklyn jail since U.S. forces seized them from their Caracas home in a middle-of-the-night raid in early January and brought them to New York.

In separate papers filed Wednesday, lawyers for Flores said she too has immunity from U.S. prosecution on sovereign immunity grounds.

"It is an attribute of Venezuela's sovereignty, and only Venezuela may surrender it," her lawyers wrote.

Maduro's lawyers said that even if Maduro were not entitled to sovereign immunity as the head of state, the case against him must be dismissed because he is also entitled to conduct-based sovereign immunity.

Meanwhile, the lawyers argued, Maduro "vehemently denies the allegations against him."

"If this case were to proceed to trial, it would be apparent that he has been falsely accused," they said.

Both have pleaded not guilty in a criminal case first brought six years ago against numerous alleged co-conspirators. They face potential life prison sentences if a jury agrees that they were part of a conspiracy to send cocaine into the U.S.

Federal prosecutors are scheduled to file a response to the arguments later this month.

President Donald Trump's administration has defended the raid to capture Maduro as a "surgical law enforcement operation." Maduro has called himself a prisoner of war and his capture a kidnapping.

U.S. prosecutors say Maduro carried out a conspiracy to move thousands of tons of cocaine into the U.S. by colluding with Venezuelan law enforcement to help drug kingpins.

title: Hospitals say coming Trump administration rules are worse than GOP's Medicaid cuts
description: Hospitals have launched a lobbying blitz to stave off Trump administration rules they say will lose them hundreds of billions of dollars.
fullText:
Hospitals thought losing hundreds of billions in Medicaid funding through GOP-led cuts last year was bad. But coming regulations from the Trump administration could slash their funding even deeper than Congress did.

Two recently proposed rules from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services would cost hospitals hundreds of billions of dollars more, hospital executives told POLITICO. The rules, which target taxes states use to get more federal Medicaid dollars — and which yield higher payments to hospitals — have prompted hospitals to launch another major lobbying blitz after record spending last year.

"Our core message to CMS is to stick to the statute. Congress cut enough," said Robert Nelb, director of policy at America's Essential Hospitals, which represents hospitals serving large Medicaid populations.

"There's no need to cut any more out of the Medicaid system at a time when the safety net is really struggling," Nelb added.

If the rules are finalized and they lose hundreds of billions on top of Congress' funding cuts, hospitals say they'll be forced to reduce services, lay off workers, consolidate operations or shutter entirely. Some systems are already doing so, telling POLITICO they've cut staff, ended contracts and slashed hospital beds in response to predicted losses.

States fund Medicaid by putting in some of their own money, which the federal government then matches. Congress cracked down on a practice in which states boost their federal matching funds by taxing hospitals to inflate the state portion of the Medicaid budget and then kick the money back to the hospitals in the form of higher payments.

Congress also restricted how states directed payments to certain providers, such as boosting payments for those in rural areas.

Hospitals say CMS' rules restricting state taxes and payments go further than what Congress intended.

Hospitals expected to lose $340 billion through 2034 after Congress passed the One Big, Beautiful Bill Act last year. If the rules are finalized as proposed, they would generate $756 billion in savings to the federal government and $265 billion in savings to states through 2035.

Or as hospitals see it, they're losing $681 billion more than they expected.

CMS said in a statement to POLITICO it will review comments for the rules before they are finalized. The agency has previously said the rule changes are necessary to rein in misused Medicaid dollars.

"Misaligned payment incentives and opaque financing arrangements are driving up costs without delivering better care," CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz said in a May press release.

title: Chargers Add Weapon With Experience in Mike McDaniel’s Offense
description: The Los Angeles Chargers have been busy rounding out their roster. They are about a week and a half away from kicking off the 2026 season in a Week 1 home matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. The Chargers put an emphasis on improving the offense from last season, adding several new interior offensive linemen, tight […] The post Chargers Add Weapon With Experience in Mike McDaniel’s Offense appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Chargers have been busy rounding out their roster.

They are about a week and a half away from kicking off the 2026 season in a Week 1 home matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. The Chargers put an emphasis on improving the offense from last season, adding several new interior offensive linemen, tight ends, and hiring Mike McDaniel to be their offensive coordinator.

ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported Los Angeles acquired Wease Jr. after the Miami Dolphins waived him this past weekend. Wease Jr. played for McDaniel in 2025, signing with Miami as an undrafted free agent following the draft.

Wease Jr. spent nearly the entire season on the Dolphins' practice squad, but saw regular season action in each of the final three games. During that span he caught 6 passes for 139 yards and 1 touchdown — which was a 63-yarder against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Wease Jr. couldn't secure a spot on Miami's 53-man roster in 2026, but reuniting with McDaniel may best for him. He began his collegiate career at Oklahoma, but played his best ball at Missouri in 2023 and 2024. In 26 games with the Tigers, Wease Jr. recorded 109 receptions for 1,566 yards and 10 touchdowns.

It should be a safe bet that the Chargers will be more explosive on offense in 2026. McDaniel is one of the best offensive minds in football, and he has more to work with in Los Angeles than he did with the Dolphins.

Quentin Johnston leads the Chargers WR corps and could be poised to have his biggest season yet. He has posted at least 700 receiving yards and 8 touchdowns each of the past two seasons. Still just 24 years old, it's reasonable to believe we have yet to see the best version of Johnston.

Ladd McConkey should have a bounce-back year in 2026 after regressing a bit in 2025. It's not like he had a bad year, recording 66 catches for 789 yards and 6 touchdowns, but expectations were definitely higher. McDaniel will likely move McConkey all around the offense and utilize his versatility.

Tre' Harris, Derius Davis, KeAndre Lambert-Smith, and Brenen Thompson round out the Chargers' WR room. Harris should have an increased role after a quite rookie year. Thompson possesses blazing speed, something McDaniel has plenty of experience with after coaching Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle in Miami. Lambert-Smith has shown a good rapport with quarterback Justin Herbert.

title: Tatsuya Imai's latest adjustment in roller-coaster first season with Astros: Calling his own pitches
description: Tatsuya Imai called his own pitches for the first time this season, a fun but practical experiment as the Astros seek better results from their biggest offseason addition.
fullText:
Late in a season of new experiences for Tatsuya Imai came another. In his relief outing Tuesday night, the Houston Astros right-hander wore a PitchCom transmitter on his glove and called his own pitches at times during his three innings against the White Sox. Manager Joe Espada said Imai had "played around" with PitchCom before, but Imai said it was his first time calling pitches in a game this season.

Imai, through interpreter Shio Enomoto, said Wednesday that calling his own pitches "felt like playing a video game" and was "really fun," but the experiment also had a practical purpose.

"When I got the ball from the catcher, I would just press (the button) right away, so I know what pitch I want to throw," Imai said. "And by doing that, I will have time after catching the ball so I can take a breath, think about it and then try to commit to the pitch. That's one reason why I've chosen to try to play around and see how it goes."

Among the adjustments for Imai to his first season in Major League Baseball was the pitch timer, which is not used in Nippon Professional Baseball. Imai said Wednesday that "timing is really important for me" on the mound and he "didn't care about the pitch clock as much as I usually do" in his outing against the White Sox. Espada indicated the pitch-calling trial was a collaborative decision.

"Just more to take control of his outings, lean on his strengths, trust his stuff," Espada said. "The information that we give him, use it apply it to your style. So we're trying to just encourage him to try some new things, and he was open to it."

For Imai and the Astros, it indicates that efforts to adapt continue near the end of a season that has not unfolded as either side hoped. Imai's outing late in a 5-1 loss Tuesday was his first since Aug. 20. He pitched in three games in August for the Astros, who guaranteed the right-hander $54 million last winter and have relegated him to the most sparing of usage amid a playoff race.

Difficulty adjusting has defined Imai's first season with the Astros, who had never signed a player directly from NPB in Japan. Difference in the baseball and pitching mounds, travel and off-field timings, and how best to deploy his arsenal have all been issues raised by or with Imai this season. The latter makes giving him the chance to call his pitches, and the comfort that might offer, intriguing.

Unclear is how often he will get that opportunity the rest of the season. When the Astros moved Imai to the bullpen at the end of July, Espada said the move was "for now." But even with their rotation in flux last month, Imai did not return to it, and all but one of his four relief outings have occurred late in games Houston trailed. He has a 5.35 ERA and a 14.9% walk rate in 70 ⅔ innings.

"I think that I haven't been able to help out the team throughout the season, and I think that's the most important part," Imai said Wednesday when asked what he envisions for the rest of his first MLB season. "So just try to make sure that I'm able to perform well and help out the team, that's the only thing. As soon as I have the opportunity, I just want to help out the team."

His first outing in 11 days Tuesday occurred with the Astros' bullpen limited and the team trailing 3-0 in the seventh inning. Imai allowed two runs over three innings, walked three and struck out five. It left him 9 ⅓ innings shy of an 80-inning plateau that would trigger a $2 million salary increase for the final two seasons of his deal. Imai has player options for each season.

The potential of this partnership continuing does infuse Imai's remaining outings this season with some significance, even as he remains stowed in the bullpen. The Astros called up prospect Ethan Pecko last month, recalled Ronel Blanco from Triple-A to start Tuesday and have used Cristian Javier as a starter or bulk reliever despite his 6.45 ERA, all illustrating Imai's standing on their pitching staff.

Thus a wrinkle like the PitchCom trial, another avenue to explore in the sides' ongoing search for results.

"It's my first year - I'm going to different ballparks, different cities, everything is the first time, so I have to just adjust," Imai said. "I want to just go throughout the day, not waste time, try to adjust and just try to perform well. But mental-wise, I'm doing good. If I pitch or not, I just have to be ready whenever, even for next season, or this season as well. I just have to be ready and just get used to it and make sure that I can perform how everybody expects."

There's more to Houston with the Chronicle.

title: Jed York, 49ers' brass are making plans in advance of potential suspension
description: With 49ers owner Jed York facing a potential suspension as a result of his recent no-contest plea on charges arising from a recent prostitution arrest in Ohio, the powers-that-be are making plans now in the event York isn't available later.
fullText:
With 49ers owner Jed York facing a potential suspension as a result of his recent no-contest plea on charges arising from a recent prostitution arrest in Ohio, the powers-that-be are making plans now in the event York isn't available later.

"Let's have conversations beforehand so that we know exactly where his wishes are," G.M. John Lynch recently told Tim Kawakami of The TK Show, via 49ersWebZone.com. "And you can't do that for everything because issues come up, like [the] trade deadline. You don't know until you know, and there's so many factors that go into that. But we'll be prepared for everything because we've put in the work, we've put in the communication beforehand."

Even without a suspension, the dynamic has changed. York moved from California to Youngstown. He's not around like he used to be.

"If he's not going to be here, Jed, we've got to talk on a regular basis," Lynch said. "He knows that, we know that, we've done that. Now, to the regularity that we normally do, because conversations kind of come up organically, no, but it's probably led to a lot more scheduled meetings where, in the past, it was more organic.

"Yesterday morning, [coach] Kyle [Shanahan] and I were on a Zoom with Jed and had a great discussion about a variety of things. And so that communication is critical, I think, to keep everybody on the same page. And Jed, he's been a great sounding board over the years. He trusts us."

It's not ideal, and it illustrates the value of having ownership who is in the building every day — but who doesn't excessively meddle in the football operation. It appears that the 49ers had found a sweet spot previously, when York lived and worked in the area. Now, it's different. He's not there on a regular basis.

And, if/when he's suspended, Lynch and Shanahan won't have access to York at all (absent burner phones).

Whether that makes this better or worse won't be known until it happens. For now, the only certainty is that it is, and will be, different.

title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels Trashed by Ravens Rookie
description: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels trashed by Baltimore Ravens rookie in viral video. The post Commanders QB Jayden Daniels Trashed by Ravens Rookie appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
It's safe to say, at this point, Baltimore Ravens rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane has a maturity issue.

While that knowledge might come with age and — hopefully — a lengthy NFL career, right now it's about to cause some headaches for Lane and, possibly, his teammates, coaches, and the Ravens' front office as they're inevitably asked about his latest faux pas.

Riding shotgun in a car driven by Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love with Washington Commanders rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams riding in the backseat, Lane goes out of his way to praise Ravens quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler "Snoop" Huntley while taking multiple shots at Washington Commanders starting quarterback Jayden Daniels.

Daniels and Huntley both wear the No. 5 jersey.

"We got the best dual-threat quarterback in the league… what?" Lane says.

"Lamar Jackson, the best in the world, are you crazy?" Lane says. "Snoop … 5 … I'm taking my 5 over your 5."

"No, you're not," Williams says.

"Yes I am," Lane says. "I'm taking Tyler Huntley over the Commanders' quarterback, every time."

Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane tells Jeremiyah Love that Tyler Huntley is better than Jayden Daniels. 😂👌 pic.twitter.com/lPOwYrgu0C

— Ravens Nation 𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀 (@LiveRavenNation) September 2, 2026

The Ravens appear to have added a player with 1st-round talent in the 3rd round (No. 60 overall) with Lane, who has already established himself as the Ravens WR2 behind Pro Bowler Zay Flowers.

"There's a lot to work with having Ja'Kobi Lane," ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. said after the pick went in.

The proof that Lane, 6-foot-4 and 205 pounds, wasn't just a Training Camp Hero came in the Ravens' preseason opener against the Philadelphia Eagles, when he put those same skills on display — including a thrilling, 16-yard touchdown catch in the 1st quarter, followed by an awkward touchdown dance.

"A familiar sight of the summer for the Ravens — Ja'Kobi Lane in the end zone," ESPN's Jamison Hensley wrote on his official X account. "What stands out here is how Lane immediately drives to the end zone after making the catch. It's a 16-yard TD for the impressive rookie third-round pick … the star of training camp shines in the preseason opener."

title: CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens could force Cowboys into franchise-altering  choice
description: The Cowboys have one of the NFL’s most dangerous receiving duos in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but Stephen Jones admits keeping both stars could create a massive financial challenge.
fullText:
CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens could force Cowboys into franchise-altering choice originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Dallas Cowboys have constructed one of the NFL's most dangerous receiving tandems. Keeping it together beyond 2026 could prove much more difficult.

CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens give quarterback Dak Prescott two legitimate No. 1 options, but executive vice president Stephen Jones acknowledged Dallas could eventually face a difficult financial decision.

"I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market," Jones said on the DLLS Cowboys podcast. "So that's gonna be a real difficult situation as we move forward."

For now, Dallas has pushed that conversation into 2027.

Pickens is playing the 2026 season on the $27.298 million franchise tag after producing 1,429 receiving yards and nine touchdowns last season. Rather than immediately committing to another massive contract, the Cowboys want the 25-year-old to put together consecutive productive seasons.

Pickens, meanwhile, has seemingly embraced the opportunity.

"George is really wanting to put back-to-back years on top of one another so it'll help his market," Jones said.

That's where Dallas' potential problem begins.

Lamb already carries one of the NFL's richest receiver contracts, averaging $34 million with three years remaining. If Pickens delivers another elite season, his asking price could climb into similar territory.

Teams have successfully invested heavily in two receivers. Cincinnati has done so with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, though carrying two premium contracts at the position requires significant salary-cap maneuvering.

Dallas isn't worrying about that yet.

The Cowboys instead appear focused on maximizing their current championship window. Prescott has Lamb and Pickens on the outside, tight end Jake Ferguson provides another established target, and Ryan Flournoy gives Dallas additional depth.

The combination could create matchup problems throughout the NFC.

But every big Pickens performance this season could simultaneously increase the price of keeping him.

Dallas wanted another year of evidence before making a long-term commitment.

If Pickens delivers it, the Cowboys could enter next offseason facing exactly the kind of expensive decision Jones already knows is coming.

title: Angels’ Outfield Depth in Trouble After Josh Lowe Injury Scratch
description: The Los Angeles Angels scratched outfielder Josh Lowe from Wednesday's game against the New York Yankees with neck stiffness. The post Angels’ Outfield Depth in Trouble After Josh Lowe Injury Scratch appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Angels scratched outfielder Josh Lowe from Wednesday's game against the New York Yankees with neck stiffness.

The Angels' outfield is severely lacking in depth, as they currently have just four outfielders listed on their active roster—one of whom is Lowe. Wade Meckler will move over to right field to cover for Lowe, with Jose Siri getting the start in left field.

Lowe, an offseason acquisition from the Tampa Bay Rays, has been with the Angels for nearly the entire season, only being away from the team during a month-long stint in Triple-A. He can play any position across the outfield, providing valuable depth in each position for the Halos.

The 28-year-old has 10 homers on the year, driving in 27 runs through 95 games this season. He has a .625 OPS this season, which would be the lowest mark of his career if he finishes the season at this pace.

His best stretch of baseball came after the Angels recalled him from Triple-A in June, where he went 8-for-18 through his final six games of June. He hit a homer and drove in four runs during that stretch, posting an OPS north of 1.000 during his hot streak.

Siri, Meckler and Mike Trout are the only other players explicitly listed as outfielders on the Angels' roster, though they have other players who could stand in if needed.

Other than Lowe, Siri, Meckler and Trout, the Angels have a few options if they need to bring someone into the outfield later in the year.

Kyren Paris came up from Triple-A Tuesday for the Angels' September call-ups, and he has plenty of experience in the outfield despite primarily playing in the middle of the infield. 2024 first-round pick Christian Moore also primarily plays in the infield, but the Angels tested him out in left field when they called him up earlier in the season.

Lastly, Adam Frazier has spent some time in the outfield this season for the Angels, and could fill in if needed.

Even still, the Angels' outfield is running extremely thin, and remains an area they'll have to reinforce come the offseason.

title: Sabalenka storms into US Open third round as Pegula, Medvedev advance
description: Aryna Sabalenka took the next step on the road to a rare US Open three-peat, routing qualifier Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1 to join a raft of contenders cruising into the third round on Wednesday.World number one Sabalenka, without a title since her impressive Indian Wells-Miami double in March was in attack mode as she overpowered 160th-ranked Russian qualifier Iatcenko in just 53 minutes.
fullText:
Aryna Sabalenka took the next step on the road to a rare US Open three-peat, routing qualifier Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1 to join a raft of contenders cruising into the third round on Wednesday.

Men's defending champion Carlos Alcaraz was seeking to join them when he took on Portugal's Jaime Faria in the nightcap on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Alcaraz won his seventh major title at the Australian Open in January but arrived in New York an unknown quantity after a wrist injury forced a four-month layoff that saw him miss Roland Garros and Wimbledon.

He dispelled doubts with a straight-sets first-round victory over Roman Safiullin and will look for further improvement against 72nd-ranked Faria.

World number one Sabalenka, without a title since her impressive Indian Wells-Miami double in March was in attack mode as she overpowered 160th-ranked Russian qualifier Iatcenko in just 53 minutes.

The Belarusian star belted 24 winners, showcasing not only her power from the baseline but also an effective touch at the net.

She dropped just four points on serve in the opening set and was broken just once to give Iatcenko her only game of the second set. Sabalenka responded by winning the next three to secure the win.

"Happy with the level I played today, happy with the focus," said Sabalenka, who will face Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova for place in the round of 16.

Jessica Pegula and former champion Daniil Medvedev also raced into the third round.

World number three Pegula needed just 56 minutes to trounce Sofia Kenin, the former Australian Open champion now ranked 110th, 6-3, 6-1.

Seventh-seeded Medvedev downed US wild card Sebastian Gorzny 6-1, 6-3, 7-5.

Pegula, who is among a trio of players who could supplant Sabalenka atop the world rankings in New York, dropped just seven points on serve.

"I was just trying to stay focused on what I needed to do," said the 2024 US Open runner-up, who next meets another former finalist in Canadian Leylah Fernandez - a 6-4, 6-1 winner over Thailand's Mananchaya Sawangkaew 6-4, 6-1.

Medvedev, who has struggled in the hard court build-up to the year's final Grand Slam, dominated 731st-ranked Gorzny.

He fired 14 aces and saved the lone break point he faced, although he was distracted briefly when a pair of small birds perched on the Louis Armstrong Stadium net and he was forced to replay a point he thought he'd won.

"I saw them straight away and I thought the point would stop straight away and we didn't," Medvedev said. "And the moment I hit the winner we stop. I was not happy with the decision."

Eighth-seeded Ben Shelton prevailed in a tense battle with former world number six Hubert Hurkacz 6-3, 5-7, 7-6 (7/3), 7-5.

"I thought it was a battle to the end," Shelton said. "I thought Hubi played fantastic today."

American 11th seed Frances Tiafoe was also in action. But another American tipped as a contender -- in-form 16th-seed Brandon Nakashima -- bowed out, upset by 46th-ranked compatriot Alex Michelsen 6-3, 6-4, 6-4.

Outside the covered confines of Ashe and the Louis Armstrong Stadium, rain again disrupted play.

Sixth-seeded Australian Alex de Minaur finally got his campaign underway in a match postponed from Tuesday but had to wait out another mid-match rain delay on the way to a 6-2, 6-2, 6-4 first-round victory over Italian Andrea Guerrieri.

Lucky loser Bu Yunchaokete of China pulled off a first-round upset, toppling 12th-seeded Spaniard Rafael Jodar 6-2, 6-1, 6-1.

title: CEO and President of Good Good no longer with company after weekslong ad scandal
description: It appears that the Good Good Golf saga is circling towards a conclusion. On Wednesday, a report from Lucia Moses at Business Insider revealed an internal memo that was shared to Good Good employees which noted that co-founder and CEO Matt Kendrick “decided to step down,” and relatively new Good Good president Joe Flannery “has…
fullText:
It appears that the Good Good Golf saga is circling towards a conclusion.

On Wednesday, a report from Lucia Moses at Business Insider revealed an internal memo that was shared to Good Good employees which noted that co-founder and CEO Matt Kendrick "decided to step down," and relatively new Good Good president Joe Flannery "has chosen to part ways as well."

For those who have been blessedly, relatively unaware of this story until now, a quick recap. Good Good Golf is a YouTube channel turned all-around golf brand that was one of the biggest success stories in the sport's social media space. Good Good had partnerships across golf brands, sold plenty of merch, and had even was set to sponsor a PGA Tour this fall.

Two weeks ago, an ad produced by Good Good for a new driver cobranded with Callaway was released over Callaway's social channels. That ad depicted Garrett Clark, one of the founders of Good Good, tackling a woman who dared to touch his driver. The reaction to the ad was immediate and obvious, as none of the brands working alongside Good Good wanted to be associated with violence against women in defense of a golf club. Callaway quickly pulled the ad.

An initial apology missed the mark, and crucially, did not break down just where in the chain of command things fell apart to allow such a bad idea to go public. From there, more apologies followed. Clark posted an eight-minute long front-facing video apology to social media explaining that the ad was meant to be a parody of the film Obsession.

"Once I watched it back and it got posted, my skin was crawling. I was cringing," Clark said in the video. "I thought it was the worst ad known to man."

It wasn't enough to stem the bleeding of partners and sponsorships, as many of the brands tied to Good Good decided it was better to part ways than stick with the brand through the struggle. Those departures were followed by a late-night social media post from Kendrick, in which he said that Callaway had approved the ad and then dropped them in "a coordinated media blitz."

Since then, people have been fired at both Callaway and Good Good in relation to the ad's release, but the departures of Kendrick and Flannery are the clearest signs yet that Good Good is looking to truly move past the situation and turn the page.

As Matt Yoder wrote for us earlier this week, the downfall of Good Good is a case study in how not to handle a crisis that will be studied for quite some time.

He came out after six innings and 83 pitches because we need him for the rest of the month. Very happy with John and Pete for doing that (not that it […]
fullText:
Let's start by saying that Dylan Cease was excellent tonight. Four hits, no runs against, no walks and four strikeouts. He came out after six innings and 83 pitches because we need him for the rest of the month. Very happy with John and Pete for doing that (not that it was a tough choice).

The offense really showed up today. We scored:

One in the first: Brett Bateman singled to start the game. And, an out later, Vladimir Guerrero doubled him home (a sign of things to come).

Five in the second: With one out, Ernie Clement singled (nice to see, he's had a tough time of it lately). Ernie stole second. Then Andrés Giménez singled him to third. Myles Straw walked to load the bases. Bateman hit into a 3-2 force at the plate. George Springer hit a soft grounder to short, that SS Angel Genao fielded and then threw 5-10 feet over the head of the second baseman. That scored two more. And Vlad homered, 3 more RBI.

One in the third: With one out, Nathan Lukes singled. Clement hit one to third; they got the runner at second and threw to first. The call on the field was out, but it was overturned on a Jays Challenge. It was very close; I didn't think they would make the change. Giménez singled. And Straw doubled, bringing in a run. 7-0.

Two in the sixth: With one out, Straw singled, Bateman walked, and Springer doubled. 8-0. And Vlad singled, 9-0.

One in the eighth: Josh Smith homered. 10-0.

One in the ninth: Sean Keys singled and went to second on a Kirk ground out. Charles McAdoo singled, putting runners on the corners. And Lukes singled, bringing in run number 11.

We had 15 hits. Vlad had 3 and 5 RBI (they took him out of the game to rest him for an early game tomorrow, so he didn't get a shot at the cycle). Lukes, Giménez and Straw had two each. The only starter with an 0 for was Okamoto (0 for 4 with 3 strikeouts). Oka had an error too, on a high pop-up that Cease was under, and then was called off. Kasuma just didn't get there in time.

The pen did the job too. Paul Sewald, Brendon Little and Braydon Fisher each had a scoreless inning.

Jays of the Day: Vlad (0.25 WPA), Springer (0.13) and Cease (0.11)

Tomorrow is an early game. 1:00 Eastern. José Soriano (2-1, 4.13 with the Jays) vs. Tanner Bibee (5-14, with a 3.88).

title: Clippers Send Angry Letter To Adam Silver After Shocking Ruling
description: The Los Angeles Clippers finally got an answer on the NBA's cap circumvention investigation, but it's not the one they were hoping for. Despite claiming innocence and complying with the league throughout the process, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver came down with strict penalties, including a $30 million fine, the loss of five draft picks, and
fullText:
The Los Angeles Clippers finally got an answer on the NBA's cap circumvention investigation, but it's not the one they were hoping for. Despite claiming innocence and complying with the league throughout the process, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver came down with strict penalties, including a $30 million fine, the loss of five draft picks, and suspensions for several Clippers executives.

Instead of accepting their losses, however, the Clippers plan to fight with everything they have. After making their initial statement today, they shared their official email to the Commissioner, in which they called him out on the way this investigation was conducted. According to the Clippers, they worked tirelessly to comply with the league office, committing millions of dollars and many hours to prove their innocence.

"Almost one year ago today, you announced that the league would be investigating podcast allegations that the Los Angeles Clippers engaged in salary cap circumvention by funneling money to Kawhi Leonard through a 'no-show' contract with a Clippers sponsor, Aspiration. In announcing that investigation, you represented that 'due process' and 'a fundamental sense of fairness' would govern the process. You made clear that the 'burden [would be] on the league' to prove any violation through actual evidence, not 'mere appearances.' And you concluded by promising that everyone involved in the investigation would be treated 'the same way I would want to be treated if people were making allegations against me.'"

"Unfortunately, none of those promises have been kept. In the last year, Steve Ballmer has spent nearly $50 million funding an investigation by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz that has stretched far beyond the bounds of what the league set out to investigate, let alone the bounds of 'fundamental fairness.' The Clippers have produced more than 30,000 documents and provided more than 20 witnesses who have sat for 30 interviews."

"Third parties, including Clippers business partners and sponsors, have likewise provided documents, interviews, and statements to investigators. Mr. Ballmer has reimbursed the costs of at least six law firms, many of which were hired at the demand of the league's lawyers. To say the investigation has been a distraction would be an understatement—Clippers employees have spent thousands of hours scouring document repositories, phones, messaging systems, central files, and accounting records, working with counsel, and sitting for interviews. This investigation has permanently strained relationships with key Clippers stakeholders."

It's more than money and picks that the Clippers have lost. Ballmer's reputation has also taken a hit, and relations with stakeholders have been severely strained. What's worse is that the Clippers claim they were given no warning about the NBA's ruling. Up until recently, they had the impression that they'd be cleared of wrongdoing, only to be convicted without the opportunity to respond right away.

"Mr. Ballmer's reputation has been irreparably damaged as he now finds himself embroiled not only in this heavily biased investigation but in civil litigation, the Aspiration bankruptcy proceeding, and more. It seems increasingly likely that Mr. Ballmer will spend years defending himself and the team against a podcaster's baseless claims. We have already detailed for Wachtell our concerns about the ways in which this process was designed to substantiate a predetermined outcome. But suffice it to say that you would not want to be treated the way that Mr. Ballmer and Clippers personnel have been treated during the past year. To what end?"

"League counsel has acknowledged in our discussions that the league does not believe there was an agreement between the Clippers and Aspiration to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard. League counsel also agreed with the Department of Justice, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and a federal judge that Mr. Ballmer was a victim of Joe Sanberg's fraud—not a participant. Nonetheless, with less than an hour's warning and no opportunity to respond, the league has issued a report and accompanying press release purporting to conclude the exact opposite of what it has said privately. None of this comports with any fundamental sense of fairness."

The Clippers did not directly funnel money to Kawhi Leonard through these endorsement deals, but they were still far too involved in helping him secure revenue outside of his NBA contract, including no-show endorsement deals with Aspiration and Daktronics, companies once associated with Ballmer and the Clippers. According to the Clips, however, their involvement in those deals (which they call introductions) is completely legal and not outside the norm, suggesting other teams and players might have similar arrangements. They even cited the NBA's previous investigation from several years ago, which failed to find any evidence against them.

"Instead, the league is intent on punishing Mr. Ballmer and the Clippers based on an entirely new theory: that the Clippers introduced Kawhi Leonard, at his request, to certain team vendors and sponsors. Wachtell has known about these introductions for months, yet raised them only at the eleventh hour—a pivot that demonstrates the league's predetermined decision to reach an adverse finding here. But more importantly, and as you well know, such introductions are both proper and commonplace in the league. We are confident that if the league spent $50 million investigating any team, it would find plenty of instances of team personnel making introductions to both sponsors and vendors in response to player requests."

"That is unsurprising because no league rule prohibits teams from making such introductions. Indeed, the Clippers' agreement to introduce Kawhi Leonard to team sponsors and vendors was the subject of a league investigation conducted more than seven years ago—an investigation that was concluded with no penalty or finding of wrongdoing. And as you know, high-ranking league officials, including Rick Buchanan, knew the Clippers were making introductions like these, in response to a player's requests, and raised no concerns about that approach."

"There is no due process in relitigating the league's prior investigation and finding fault with behavior that the league knew about back in 2019. And retroactively punishing the Clippers for violating a rule that never existed is hardly consistent with due process."

Finally, the Clippers conclude their email with a clear and powerful show of resistance. They accuse the investigation of being heavily flawed, call out the league for not giving them a heads-up on the decision, and announce their plans to fight back with everything they have.

"This investigation has been flawed from the outset. And your decision to issue this report without any notice to the Clippers or their counsel is inexcusable. This type of witch hunt flies in the face of fundamental fairness and of the integrity of the league and of this sport that we all love. We are exploring every legal remedy to address this gross injustice."

It's clear from this lengthy email that the Clippers have no intention of accepting the NBA's ruling here. They continue to claim their innocence and take issue with how this entire investigation has played out. But after a years-long quest to discover the truth, Adam Silver is showing no signs of reversing his decision, and it raises questions as to how far the Clippers will go to avoid the crippling list of penalties.

title: Brett Baty, Nick Morabito each tally three RBI in Mets' 10-4 series-clinching win over Rays
description: The New York Mets (63-77) took the rubber match of their three-game road series against the Tampa Bay Rays (83-56), 10-4, the final score, thanks to heroics from Brett Baty and Nick Morabito.
fullText:
The Mets (63-77) took the rubber match of their three-game road series against the Tampa Bay Rays (83-56), 10-4, the final score.

-- The Amazins wasted no time taking an early lead over Rays right-handed starter Griffin Jax. Juan Soto reached base on a single up the middle, but was retired on a fielder's choice by Bo Bichette. Carson Benge walked to put runners on first and second with two outs, and Jared Young capitalized with an RBI single. Tampa catcher Liam Hicks couldn't hold onto the ball when applying the late tag on Bichette, and the ball skittered away. The error allowed Benge to score and Young to move up to second base on the play. Marcus Semien added to the damage with a double down the left field line to bring Young across home plate, and the Mets were up 3-0.

-- The Mets engineered another two-out rally in the third inning. They loaded the bases after A.J. Ewing hustled out an infield single, and Brett Baty capitalized with a big opposite-field swing which ricocheted off the very top of the wall in left-center field, clearing the bases and knocking Jax out of the game.

-- 29-year-old righty Justin Hagenman was called on to make the start for the Mets on Wednesday, marking his first MLB appearance of the season. He threw 46 pitches, allowed two hits, walked one batter, and allowed one earned run while striking out two over three full innings.

-- Right-handed reliever Chris Devenski came in for Hagenman, and had a nightmare outing. After recording two outs in the fourth inning, Devenski unraveled, allowing three earned runs on three hits, including a two-run homer off the bat of Richie Palacios. Taylor Walls extended the inning with a double to force Mets interim skipper Andy Green to call on Dedniel Núñez to strand the runner in scoring position and hold the Mets' 6-4 lead.

-- Bichette led off the seventh inning with a double off the foot of the wall in right-center field. With the bases loaded and nobody out, rookie left fielder Nick Morabito stepped into the box for his first turn at the plate. He cleared the bases with a looping line drive into the left-field corner, his first career hit.

-- The Mets wouldn't relinquish their lead, and closed out the final three frames of the ballgame without surrendering a run thanks to strong relief pitching from Nate Lavender, Daniel Duarte, and Jonathan Pintaro. Along the way, Soto mashed a solo shot, his 23rd round-tripper on the season, to extend New York's lead to 10-4.

Baty began the game as the eighth batter in the Mets' order, and his three-run double padded the team's early cushion. Mark Vientos pinch-hit for Baty to face left-handed reliever Cam Booser and stroked a single. Morabito pinch-ran for Vientos and, in his first time at the plate, faced right-handed reliever Manuel Rodriguez, and he replicated Baty's earlier feat with yet another two-out three-run double, a moment he'll cherish for a lifetime. Morabito kept his momentum rolling in the ninth inning with a line drive single.

Collectively, the eighth man in the Mets lineup batted 4-for-5 with six RBI on the night.

23 FOR 22.

The Mets travel to San Francisco to take on the Giants in a three-game series, with first pitch for Friday's game set for 7:10 p.m. EST.

New York will send out Nolan McLean (3.06 ERA, 1.12 WHIP in 155.2 IP).

The Giants have not yet announced their starter.

title: Shohei Ohtani injury update adds confusion to perplexing status
description: Shohei Ohtani is expected to have an impact on the postseason as the Los Angeles Dodgers continue their quest for a World Series three-peat.
fullText:
Shohei Ohtani is expected to have an impact on the postseason as the Los Angeles Dodgers continue their quest for a World Series three-peat.

What opportunities Ohtani might have to make an impact remain uncertain.

Ohtani appeared to be trending in the right direction with his pitching progression, but that was put to a halt on Aug. 29. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced that the team's two-way star would not be making a return as it was anticipated. The pitcher had thrown a 20-pitch bullpen just the day before.

In a Sept. 2 conversation with reporters, Roberts said the team is still considering shutting down Ohtani, but the Dodgers aren't ready to make that decision.

"I know he is in lockstep with (Mark Prior), the pitching guys, the training staff, but I think for me he has to throw a bullpen, then we will see the next progression," Roberts said.

Ohtani is expected to remain available as a designated hitter, but hasn't taken the mound as a pitcher in a game since July 3 due to knee inflammation and biceps discomfort.

Ohtani did not pitch during his first season with the Dodgers, after needing a full year to recover from right elbow surgery.

Roberts was also asked about the possibility of Ohtani playing in the outfield, but the manager declared that's "not on the table."

The Dodgers have not officially shut down Ohtani as a pitcher for the rest of the season. If and when he is cleared and ready to pitch, Ohtani could see limited action on a pitch count before working a full game.

As of Wednesday, Sept. 2, Ohtani was hitting .281 with 88 runs scored, 30 home runs and 80 RBIs in 128 games this season.

As a pitcher, Ohtani has posted an 8-2 record in 14 starts this season. He's allowed 55 hits, 21 runs (17 earned) and four home runs, while striking out 95.

title: Detroit's Orlando Lovejoy wins lawsuit for extra year, transfer coming
description: Orlando Lovejoy played two seasons at Eastern Michigan and two seasons at Detroit Mercy.
fullText:
DETROIT — Former Detroit Mercy basketball star Orlando Lovejoy is the among the latest batch of college athletes to score a legal victory in a bid to receive an extra year of eligibility.

Lovejoy was one of 40 college athletes who have been granted a temporary restraining order by a circuit court judge in Kentucky. The decision by Judge Brian C. Edwards makes Lovejoy, a highly decorated point guard, immediately eligible for a fifth season. Where that fifth season will take place remains to be seen.

His representatives from CGL Agency told The News on Wednesday that Lovejoy plans to announce a transfer destination soon, possibly as early as this week. He stands to earn six figures on the NIL market.

Kentucky football player Alex Afari, Seth Trimble, and others have both been added to the TRO that was granted in the Kentucky state court 5 in 5 case.

Afari is currently eligible to play for Kentucky.

Trimble is currently eligible to play 🏀 for Louisville. https://t.co/qNXJ4I5oCP

Lovejoy, at this point, can't return to Detroit Mercy, which has maxed out its roster with 15 scholarship players.

Lovejoy, 23, was a four-time all-state selection in high school at Summit Academy before playing his first two years of college basketball at Eastern Michigan. He transferred to Detroit Mercy, where he played the last two seasons, earning first-team all-Horizon League honors in 2025-26. In 2025-26, Lovejoy, 6-foot-3 and 190 pounds, started all 31 games and was top-10 in the Horizon League in scoring (15.8), assists (3.7), steals (1.6) and free-throw percentage (89.2).

Lovejoy also led Detroit Mercy to the Horizon League championship game, in which the Titans lost to Wright State, 66-63. The Titans led at halftime and were seeking their first NCAA Tournament since 2012.

Hundreds of college athletes have filed dozens of lawsuits against the NCAA over the past several weeks, seeking the extra year of eligibility, challenging the NCAA's June decision to give athletes a five-year window to play five seasons. The NCAA's rule shut out the high-school class of 2022 from receiving a fifth year.

Michigan's Roddy Gayle Jr. was among players who have received a TRO. Michigan has kept a roster spot open for him. Also receiving a fifth season through a court-ordered TRO was former Oakland star point guard Brody Robinson. Oakland kept a roster spot open for him in case he was able and willing to return, but he has transferred to Creighton.

Oakland still has a roster spot availabile.

title: Maryland volleyball overcomes Arkansas, 3-1
description: The Terps left the SEC/Big Ten challenge with a critical victory that sets them up for the remainder of the season.
fullText:
Fresh off of opening-night losses, Maryland women's volleyball and Arkansas stepped onto Vanderbilt's Memorial gym looking for a quick turnaround on the second day of the SEC/Big Ten Challenge. In a relentless, back-and-forth battle, the Terps prevailed with a 3-1 win.

Both teams treated Wednesday's match as a fresh opportunity to prove themselves. From the opening serve, it was a neck-and-neck battle. That momentum shaped not just the first set but the entirety of the match.

Neither team could create any separation early in what turned into a back-and-forth battle. In the opening set, the Razorbacks edged out Maryland, 26-24, capitalizing on a late set point after trading blows through the extra points.

While Maryland took an early five-point lead in the set, Arkansas clawed back behind a pair of kills from opposite hitter Romani Thurman. That sequence was part of the Razorbacks' four-point run, which allowed them to take a one-point lead, 23-22.

But it was Layla Smith's solo block and an error from Sydney Bryant that allowed Arkansas to pull away and win the first set.

The Terps responded with a similar resilience in the second set. In an extended 30-28 marathon, Maryland fended off multiple set points and matched Arkansas point-for-point before finally taking the set.

Riding that momentum, Maryland brought the energy and produced an early lead in the third set. The Terps managed to lose the point buffer that was initially set. Arkansas regained their drive momentarily by indulging in long rallies, keeping the set score tied for longer.

As the set progressed, Maryland's freshman Ava Brown begins to attract the spotlight with her constituency and skills that explain her high kill count. Ranked No. 7 in hitting percentage with a .516, Brown let the Terps take the third set with a sharp spike at the net. Setter Sara Toth repeatedly looked to the freshman on out-of-system plays, and Brown delivered by intentionally tooling the Arkansas block.

Despite being up 2-1 in sets, Maryland refused to relax during the fourth set. While both teams traded points early, the Terps eventually dominated their way throughout, building a comfortable cushion and eliminating the possibility of a potential five-set comeback from Arkansas and securing their first win of the SEC/Big Ten tournament.

With the 3-1 victory over Arkansas, Maryland moves to the 1-1 on the season and finishes the Big Ten challenge on a high note. The Terps showed remarkable growth from night one to night two, particularly in their ability to execute under pressure during tight, late-set scenarios. Maryland will look to keep that momentum rolling as they return home to host their next matchup at the XFINITY Center Pavillion back home.

1. Freshman potential. With six freshmen, this is a formative season for Maryland. The team has shown an ability to grow, even just game to game.

2. High-pressure resilience. After dropping a tight, 26-24, opening frame, Maryland could have let the momentum slip away. Instead, the Terps showed remarkable grit in the second set, fending off multiple set points in an incredible 30-28 victory.

3. Front-row defense. While the offense found its rhythm a little further into the game, Maryland's net defense anchored the victory. The Terps out-blocked Arkansas 11-7 overall, using crucial touches and blocking in Sets 3 and 4 to keep the Razorbacks' primary hitters at bay.

title: UConn Football 2026 season preview: The RB Room
description: Like most position groups, every major contributor at running back from last year is gone. Cam Edwards, Mel brown, Victor Rosa, Oliver Lundberg Coleman and MJ Flowers transferred out. Those five backs accumulated 1,870 rushing yards and 21 of the team’s 26 rushing touchdowns, with Edwards leading the way, racking up 1,240 yards and hitting […]
fullText:
Like most position groups, every major contributor at running back from last year is gone. Cam Edwards, Mel brown, Victor Rosa, Oliver Lundberg Coleman and MJ Flowers transferred out. Those five backs accumulated 1,870 rushing yards and 21 of the team's 26 rushing touchdowns, with Edwards leading the way, racking up 1,240 yards and hitting the end zone 15 times.

Despite the significant departing production, the rebuilt RB room has lots of potential playmakers. Head coach Jason Candle recruited several players with proven production and others looking to prove themselves.

"There's a couple of guys in that room that can score a 70- or 80-yard touchdown," Candle said in a recent media appearance.

Kenji Christian, Redshirt Senior

Christian started his college career at North Carolina A&T (2023-2024) before transferring to Toledo last season. As a freshman, the Alabama native contributed 718 rushing yards and six touchdowns in 11 games. He suffered a season-ending injury in Week 3 of the 2024 season.

"My coach always told me, just put everything together," Christian said. "I feel like I was always missing stuff like that. My coach kind of helped me with my process last year…taking care of my body."

Following his rehab year, Christian joined Toledo and bounced back. He was behind running back Chip Trayanum on the depth chart, but still got in on the action. In 13 appearances, the 6-foot-2, 207-pound running back carried the ball 105 times and produced 528 rushing yards for four touchdowns. He also hauled in 193 receiving yards and a touchdown last year.

"He feels like it is his time," Candle said when discussing Christian. "You can only judge off of what you've seen from January to now and until this point in time, he's done a really, really good job with that. So, I'm excited for him.

Heading into 2026, Christian ranked No. 81 on The Athletic's 2026 Freaks List.

Prior to becoming a Husky, Bowers fought his way into the FBS conference as he began his collegiate career in junior college. At Iowa Central Community College in 2024, the Pennsylvania native played 11 games, Bowers compiled 1,008 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns. He also snagged 24 receptions for 363 yards and two end zone appearances.

"I would say explosive or the home-run-hitter type," Bowers said when describing his run game.

After an incredible 2024 season, Bowers transferred to West Virginia the following year. In 10 games, the 5-foot-10, 191-pound running back notched 249 yards for two touchdowns.

"My last call was very tempo, so I'm kind of used to it. It's not anything that's out of the ordinary for me," Bowers said when discussing Candle's fast-paced offense.

Before arriving in Connecticut, Cornist attended Tulane for two years (2023-2024). In 2024, the Ohio native logged 149 rushing yards with one TD in six contests. The 5-foot-11, 210-pound running back transferred to Central Michigan for this past season, logging 470 yards and a TD in 13 appearances.

"Trey Cornist is a big guy who had a great spring. It took him maybe a couple of practices to get comfortable," Offensive Coordinator Nunzio Campanile said. "He's like a bowling ball; you don't want to tackle that guy."

Before coming to UConn, Hart experienced Campanile's coaching abilities in his two years at Syracuse (2024-2025). During his time there, Hart saw limited time in the backfield, posting 18 carries for 71 yards.

"He's a really versatile back," Campanile said. "He can do a lot of things; he can catch the ball; he can block."

Before joining UConn, Reeder spent two seasons with Northwestern (2024-2025). Last season, the South Carolina native accumulated 222 rushing yards for a touchdown.

title: Pirates Rally in Late Innings but Fall to Giants in Extras
description: PITTSBURGH — The Pirates fought back in the late innings to force extras but fell 5-4 to the Giants in […]
fullText:
PITTSBURGH — The Pirates fought back in the late innings to force extras but fell 5-4 to the Giants in the 10th on Wednesday night at PNC Park.

Top 1st, 1-0 SFG: For the second straight game, Rafael Devers homered to center. His solo blast off Bubba Chandler gave the Giants (58-82) an early lead.

Bottom 4th, 1-1: The Pirates (68-72) tied the game when Landen Roupp issued a two-out walk to Esmerlyn Valdez with the bases loaded.

Top 5th, 3-1 SFG: The Giants loaded the bases after Oneil Cruz and Valdez watched a ball fall in shallow right-center. Bryce Eldridge followed with a sacrifice fly to center and Turner Hill delivered a two-out RBI single to right.

Bottom 7th, 3-2 SFG: The Pirates put two runners in scoring position with one out against Ryan Walker. After the Giants turned to Ryan Walker, Spencer Horwitz got his team within a run on an RBI groundout to short.

Bottom 8th, 3-3: Bryan Reynolds opened the inning with a double, advanced to second on a Nick Gonzales groundout and scored on Cruz's infield single off Carson Seymour.

Top 10th, 5-3 SFG: The Giants scored a pair of runs off Camilo Doval (3-2) in the 10th. Eldridge brought home a run with a double to left field and Hill tacked on another with a sacrifice fly to right.

Bottom 10th, 5-4 SFG: Nick Gonzales opened the bottom of the 10th inning with an RBI single up the middle against Dylan Smith.

Giants left fielder Turner Hill made a smooth sliding catch in the bottom of the ninth inning to take away a potential walk-off hit from Bryan Reynolds.

Rafael Devers homered as part of a two-hit performance and scored twice, including the game-winning run in extras.

Bubba Chandler's 26 starts are the most by a Pirates rookie in a season since Paul Maholm made 30 in 2006.

Bubba Chandler: 5.0 innings, five hits, three runs, three walks, four strikeouts, 88 pitches/55 strikes

Camilo Doval: 1.0 inning, one hit, two runs (one earned), one walk, 16 pitches/10 strikes

Bryan Reynolds: 2 for 5, one doube, two runs

Oneil Cruz: 1 for 3, one walk, one RBI, one steal

Bubba Chandler allowed only his second home run over his last nine starts dating back to July 11 in the second game of a doubleheader against the Brewers.

Oneil Cruz extended his hitting streak to five games.

The Pirates fell to 6-10 in extra innings this season.

The Pirates are going with a bullpen game for the series finale. RHP Blade Tidwell (0-1, 4.54 ERA) gets the start for the Giants. First pitch: 12:35 p.m. ET on SportsNet Pittsburgh, MLB Network/100.1 FM & AM 1020.

title: Philadelphia man charged for attempted break-in at Eagles star Saquon Barkley's home in July
description: While people were home at the time of the attempted break-in, Saquon Barkley said that nobody was hurt during the incident.
fullText:
A Philadelphia man has been arrested and charged with multiple felonies after an attempted break-in at the home of Eagles star Saquon Barkley earlier this summer.

Jabir Parker, 24, was arrested on Tuesday and is facing charges related to two break-ins and the attempted break-in of a third home in the Philadelphia area this summer, according to NBC10.

The first two break-ins, per the report, were successful. Parker allegedly broke into a home on June 22 and stole roughly $107,000 worth of jewelry. A few weeks later, Parker allegedly stole more than $687,000 worth of jewelry from a second home.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

The third attempt, on July 18, was the one at Barkley's home. While officials did not name the owners of the home involved, NBC10 reported that it is owned by Barkley and his family.

"In the third burglary, the … homeowners were awakened by suspicious sounds before finding an unknown male inside the home and calling 911," the district attorney said.

Barkley told NBC10 that nobody inside the home was hurt. He has since taken up extra security.

Parker is facing multiple felonies, including burglary and conspiracy to burglary. He is still in custody as of Wednesday afternoon, and is due in court on Sept. 10.

Barkley is just the latest NFL player to be the victim of a home burglary recently. Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb had more than $300,000 worth of luxury bags stolen from his Texas home during training camp. Both Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders and Tennessee titans lineman Jeffery Simmons had their homes broken into during the 2025 season, and seven individuals were charged in February for allegedly burglarizing the homes of Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, among others.

Barkley ran for 1,140 yards and had nine total touchdowns last season, his second with the Eagles after helping them to their Super Bowl win the year before. The Eagles will open the season against the Washington Commanders on Sept. 13.

title: Mets win with offensive beatdown in Tampa Bay
description: The Rays were no match for the Mets exploding offense.
fullText:
The Mets entered Wednesday night's game with a hope to win an away series against the Rays. They had Justin Hagenman making his return to the major league roster after missing months on the 60-day injured list with a fractured rib. They would be facing Griffin Jax, also making his return from the injured list.

The Mets got off to a blazing start. They had runners on first and second with two outs, and Jared Young hit a single to right field that scored Bo Bichette as the game's first run. Liam Hicks missed the throw at the plate and the ball bounced away, allowing Carson Benge to score and Young to make it to second. Marcus Semien then hit a double to drive in Young as the Mets third run. A.J. Ewing grounded out to end the inning, but the Mets had taken a nice, roomy early lead.

After a quiet inning and a half, the Mets ignited again in the top of the third. Bichette led off with a single, then stole second after two consecutive outs. Semien walked and Ewing got an infield single to load the bases. Brett Baty hit a monster double off the wall in left field, missing a grand slam by a few feet but driving in three runs to double the Mets lead. He also drove Rays starter Griffin Jax from the game in less than three full innings, with Steven Matz coming in to get the final out and stop the bleeding for the Rays.

The Rays began trying to comeback in the bottom of the inning. With two outs, they got a walk and a single to put two runners on, and Jonathan Aranda hit an RBI single to drive in Taylor Walls as the Rays first run. Hagenman got the final out to end the inning, which was also the end of his night. He went three innings, giving up a run on two hits and a walk while collecting a pair of strikeouts.

Chris Devenski came in for the bottom of the fourth, and he had a rough go of it. A Chandler Simpson single was bookended by the first and second outs of the inning, and a pickoff attempt was unsuccessful after Simpson was deemed to not have run out of the basepath on his way back to first, and a balk was called on Devenski to allow Simpson to advance anyway. Cedric Mullins then hit a single that drove in Simpson as the Rays second run, and Benge committed a throwing error that allowed Mullins to reach second. Richie Palacios then hit a two run home run to bring the Rays within two runs. A Taylor Walls double was the end of the line for Devenski, who ended his night with three runs allowed in 0.2 innings. Dedniel Núñez came in and got the final out of the inning to allow the Mets to escape the nightmarish fourth.

Núñez ended up going 1.1 hitless innings with a strikeout, helping the Mets reach the seventh inning, where the offense exploded once again. Bichette led off with a double, and Benge followed that up with a single to move Bichette to third. Young hit into fielder's choice with Bichette being thrown out at the plate, driving Rays reliever Cam Booser from the game in favor of Manuel Rodríguez. Semien was hit by a pitch to load the bases, but Ewing struck out in what looked to be the makings of a missed opportunity for the Mets offense. But Nick Morabito, brought in to be the defensive replacement in left field, came up to the plate for the first time in the game. He ended up getting his first major league hit, a double to drive in three runs and put the Mets ahead by five runs. Rodríguez struck out Torrens to end the inning but the Mets had opened up another wide lead with little time left for the Rays to mount another comeback.

The Mets had one last run in them, coming in the top of the eighth courtesy of a Juan Soto solo home run. And the Mets bullpen, thanks to Nate Lavender, Daniel Duarte, and Jonathan Pintaro, held the Rays scoreless for the final frames. They get a day off tomorrow before returning to New York to face the San Francisco Giants in a series that starts Friday night.
